Product basics

What are Box Hubs?

Box Hubs are content portals that let you curate, organize, view, and share Box content in a centralized experience. A Hub brings together files, folders, links, and supporting context so teams can find information, understand it, and act on it without navigating many separate folders.

Which plans include Box Hubs?

Box Hubs are available for Enterprise plans and above. Box AI for Hubs is available for Enterprise Plus and Enterprise Advanced plans.

What are common Hub use cases?

Common examples include:

  • Employee onboarding resources
  • Project knowledge bases and workspaces
  • Team sites with policies, recordings, and reference materials
  • Company asset libraries and content playlists
  • Sales and marketing enablement portals
Does adding content to a Hub duplicate the files?

No. Hubs curate and present existing Box content. The same file or folder can appear in multiple Hubs without creating separate copies of the source content.

Can I set the Hubs gallery as my Box home page?

Yes. Open Account Settings > Account > General Options and choose Hubs as the Home Page.

Does Box Hubs work on mobile?

Box Hubs does not work on mobile. The Box Embed Widget is also not optimized for mobile browsers.

Creating, editing, and deleting Hubs

How do I create a Hub?

In the Box web app:

  • Open Hubs from the left navigation, or click the plus icon next to Hubs.
  • Select New Hub.
  • Enter a name and optional description.
  • Add files, folders, and content blocks.
  • Save and publish. If you omit a name, Box auto-populates Untitled Hub with a date and time. Descriptions are optional and are limited to 2000 characters.
Who can create or delete a Hub?

Only Hub Co-owners can create or delete Hubs. Editors can build and publish Hub content but cannot create, delete, or manage Hub settings.

What happens when I delete a Hub?

Collaborators lose access to the Hub experience. The source files and folders in Box are not deleted. Deletion cannot be undone.

How do I edit a Hub?

Open the Hub from the gallery and select Edit. You need Co-owner or Editor permissions. Use the Add Block panel to insert content, then save your changes.

Can I customize a Hub logo and background?

Yes. Co-owners and Editors can upload a logo and background image from the gallery, Box, or a device. Accepted formats are JPG and PNG under 5 MB. Box recommends a square logo and a background with about a 5:1 aspect ratio and a minimum width of 1600 px. Center-aligning the logo also center-aligns the Hub name and description.

Content, builder, and pages

What content blocks can I add?

Available block types include:

  • Files and Folders
  • Section Header (up to 100 characters)
  • Paragraph (up to 5000 characters)
  • Link Cards
  • Call Out (up to 5000 characters)
  • Link Preview
  • Divider You can click or drag blocks onto the page, then move, duplicate, trash, or move them to another page.
How do I add files and folders to a Hub?

You can only add files or folders owned by your enterprise, and only content where you are Owner, Co-owner, or Editor.

Common methods:

  • Use the Files and Folders picker in a new or edited Hub.
  • From Files, select items, open More Options, and choose Add to Hub.
  • From an open file, open More Options and choose Add to Hub. Newly added content appears at the top by default. The source item name does not change.
Why can an Editor not add a folder to a Hub?

The folder may have the collaboration restriction Only folder owners and co-owners can send collaborator invites and add this folder to a Hub enabled. When that setting is checked, only the folder Owner or Co-owner can add the folder to a Hub.

Have an Owner or Co-owner uncheck the restriction, add the folder themselves, or elevate the user’s folder role if appropriate.

What are Link Cards?

Link Cards are visual navigation tiles with a title, description, and optional image. They can link to Hub pages, Box content, Forms, Sign requests, file requests, or external URLs. External destinations show an external-link icon and open in a new tab.

Hub access does not automatically grant access to a card destination. Viewers without permission see the destination’s standard access error.

How do pages and nested pages work?

Pages create a hierarchy within a Hub. Use the Hub Outline panel to add pages, add nested pages, duplicate pages, drag pages to reorder or nest them, or delete pages.

The home page is always the highest page and cannot be moved. Deleting a page removes its blocks and nested pages and cannot be reversed.

How do previews behave inside a Hub?

Most document previews open in an overlay on top of the Hub. Box Notes and Box Canvas open in a new tab.

How do I notify collaborators after updating a Hub?

Choose Save > Save & Notify Collaborators, enter a message, and send. Collaborators receive an email with your message and a link to the Hub. The sender does not receive that notification. Choosing Save alone publishes the changes without emailing collaborators.

Permissions and access

What Hub permission levels exist?

Box Hubs uses four levels:

  • Admin: Enables Hubs for users or groups in the Admin Console.
  • Co-owner: Broadest Hub permissions, including create, delete, settings, content, sharing, and embeds.
  • Editor: Can manage content, collaborators when allowed, shared links when allowed, embeds, and publish, but cannot create or delete Hubs or manage Hub settings.
  • Viewer: Can view the Hub and, depending on settings, share or copy it, but cannot change the Hub.
What access do Hub collaborators get to the files inside?

Granting a user access to a Hub automatically gives Viewer permissions to the files and folders in that Hub. That automatic Viewer grant does not apply to external or Box links embedded with Link Preview or Link Cards.

If a folder Uploader is invited to a Hub as Viewer, that person’s permissions on the content become Viewer/Uploader.

Can I edit source files from a Hub when I open it through a shared link?

No. Even if you have Editor access to some files or folders, opening the Hub through a shared link does not let you edit those items from the Hub level.

Who needs a Box account to use a Hub?

Invited collaborators need a Box account on any plan. Hubs can be viewed anonymously when shared through an open shared link.

Can content owners remove their files from a Hub?

Yes. Content owners and co-owners can unlink their files or folders from a Hub from the item’s Collaborators page Hubs tab by choosing Remove Access.

Sharing and external collaboration

How do I share a Hub?

Share by inviting collaborators or creating a shared link. Hub settings and enterprise settings control who can create or modify shared links and whether public shared links are allowed. Hubs do not support an editable shared link to the Hub itself.

What Hub settings control sharing and collaboration?

Co-owners can configure:

  • Restrict collaboration to within the enterprise
  • Who can copy the Hub: no one, only users in the enterprise, or anyone
  • Who can add or modify collaborators: Editors and co-owners, or only co-owners
  • Who can create or modify shared links: Editors and co-owners, or only co-owners
  • Box AI features for the Hub Enterprise admins can set defaults and lock some of these options. Greyed-out settings usually mean an admin locked them.
What happens when I invite an external collaborator to a Hub?

The external collaborator can view the Hub content. Inviting an external collaborator automatically allows that person to view the files and folders in the Hub, even when those items have an external collaboration restriction. Hubs with external collaborators show a globe icon in the gallery and Hub header.

Shield classifications that block external collaborators can still prevent those users from seeing classified content.

Does an external collaborator need Hubs enabled in their own enterprise?

No. They can open the Hub from its URL. If Hubs is not enabled in their enterprise, they cannot open it from their own Hubs gallery.

Why does inviting an external collaborator by alias fail?

Box currently requires the collaborator’s main email address. Using an email alias returns an error that the person could not be added as a collaborator.

Are Hub collaborations listed under External Users in the Admin Console?

No. Hub collaborations are not shown in the External Users tab under Users & Groups.

Copying Hubs

Can I copy a Hub?

Yes, when copy permission allows it. Open the Hub, choose More Options > Make a Copy, name the new Hub, optionally include files and folders, and confirm.

What is included when I copy a Hub?

Included:

  • Hub name and description

  • Pages and page hierarchy

  • Logo and background image

  • Text blocks, embeds, and dividers Not included:

  • Collaborators

  • Hub settings such as copy permissions, collaboration restrictions, and shared-link settings Files and folders are optional. Only items where you have Editor, Owner, or Co-owner access are copied. File and folder blocks remain in the structure even when the items themselves are not copied; those blocks appear empty.

Can I copy a Hub from another enterprise?

Yes, if the source Hub co-owner allows Anyone to copy. The copy is created in your tenant with the same structure and text layout. Files and folders cannot be copied across enterprises, so those blocks appear empty.

Embedding and API

Can I embed a Hub in another website or portal?

Yes. Editors and Co-owners can create an embed. Open More Options, choose Embed Hub or Embed Widget, select a size, optionally hide Hubs navigation or gallery access, and copy the iframe code.

Viewers of the embed still need Hub access by invitation or shared link. The Embed Widget is not optimized for mobile browsers and may fail when third-party cookies or cross-website tracking are blocked.

Can I embed Box AI for Hubs?

If you are eligible for Box AI with Hubs, the embed experience can include an AI question-and-answer chat mode or a button that launches that chat UX.

Is there a Box Hubs API?

Yes. The Box Hubs API can create, copy, update, and delete Hubs, manage contents and collaborators, configure settings, retrieve Hub information, and allow admins to see enterprise Hubs.

Administration

How does an admin enable Box Hubs?

In Admin Console > Enterprise Settings > Content and Sharing, configure Hubs for:

  • All Hubs users
  • Selected users or groups
  • Everyone except selected users or groups
  • Or disable for all Selected-user enablement is limited to 100 names or email addresses and 100 groups. For larger audiences, enable or disable Hubs for the whole organization.

Admins can also choose whether Hubs appears in navigation for only creators or for all managed users.

Can an admin manage all enterprise Hubs?

Yes. In Admin Console > Content > Hubs, admins and permitted co-admins can review Hub name, creator, views, last viewed, updated date, co-owners, and collaborators. From there they can share, manage collaborators, open Hub settings, or delete a Hub. Co-admin permissions can be limited to viewing, or expanded to manage, share, and delete.

Can admins set enterprise defaults for Hub sharing and copying?

Yes. Admins can configure global presets for enterprise-only collaboration, public shared-link restriction, who can copy Hubs, who can manage collaborators, and who can manage shared links. They can also allow or prevent Hub co-owners from changing those defaults.

Shared-link availability and expiration can also be scoped to folders, files, and hubs.

What happens if Hubs creation is disabled but Hubs already exist?

Users can still view the Hubs gallery. To disable the product for the entire enterprise after Hubs already exist, contact Box Support.

Box AI for Hubs

What does Box AI for Hubs do?

It lets eligible users ask questions across the curated files in a Hub and receive summaries and insights with citations. Open a Hub and select the Box AI button, or use the Explore with Box AI option from a collaboration invitation email when the feature is enabled.

What are the Box AI for Hubs item limits?

Documented limits include:

  • 20,000 files per Hub
  • 10 million files across all Hubs in the organization
  • Only the first 4 MB of a document’s text representation is indexed When the per-Hub limit is exceeded, Box AI for that Hub is disabled until enough items are removed.
How long does indexing take?

Files added to a Hub may take up to an hour to index. Most files index within minutes, but larger Hubs can take longer. Retry after waiting if AI answers seem incomplete.

What content types and questions work poorly with Box AI for Hubs?

Supported types include text files and spreadsheets. Spreadsheets embedded inside text files are not supported.

Weaker or inaccurate results are documented for calculations, table structures, counting, metadata such as page numbers or authors, images, video, charts, file-name questions, and some list-style prompts. Non-English prompts can also produce lower-quality results.

What should I check if Box AI is missing from a Hub?

Confirm with an administrator that Box AI is enabled, Box AI for Hubs is enabled for the enterprise, the Hub itself allows AI, the account plan supports it, and the user can view the relevant files.

SharePoint comparison

Can Box Hubs fully replace SharePoint for document management and collaboration?

Yes, Box Hubs can serve as a SharePoint replacement for many use cases, particularly for document management, content organization, and secure collaboration. It simplifies content structure, reduces data sprawl, and provides cross-platform access without the complexities of SharePoint sites and subsites. However, organizations relying on SharePoint for intranet pages or deep Microsoft ecosystem workflows may need complementary tools.

What is the process for migrating from SharePoint to Box Hubs?

Migrating from SharePoint to Box Hubs follows these steps:

  • Assessment: Identify content that needs migration and clean up unnecessary files.
  • Planning: Map SharePoint folder structures, permissions, and metadata to Box Hubs.
  • Migration: Use Box Shuttle (Box’s official migration tool) or third-party solutions to transfer files while preserving permissions.
  • Validation: Ensure content integrity, permissions, and metadata are correctly transferred.
  • Training & Adoption: Educate teams on using Box Hubs efficiently to maximize adoption.
How does Box Hubs compare to SharePoint in terms of security and compliance?

Box is built for security and compliance-first content management, offering:

  • Zero-trust security architecture
  • Data encryption at rest and in transit
  • Advanced threat detection (Box Shield)
  • Regulatory compliance (HIPAA, FedRAMP, GDPR, FINRA, etc.) Unlike SharePoint, where compliance settings require manual configuration, Box provides enterprise-grade security by default.
How does Box Hubs handle structured content compared to SharePoint?

Box Hubs organizes content using a centralized, user-friendly structure that eliminates the site sprawl often seen in SharePoint. With features like:

  • Metadata tagging for smarter search
  • Curation of relevant content into Hubs
  • Advanced filtering and AI-powered content discovery Box Hubs makes it easier to find and manage content without relying on complex folder structures.
Does Box Hubs integrate with Microsoft 365 and Teams like SharePoint does?

Yes. Box integrates seamlessly with Microsoft 365, Teams, and Outlook, allowing users to:

  • Edit Word, Excel, and PowerPoint files in Box without downloading them.
  • Access Box content within Microsoft Teams (instead of SharePoint).
  • Send secure email attachments using Box for Outlook. While SharePoint is natively embedded in Microsoft 365, Box provides a platform-agnostic approach, ensuring flexibility across multiple ecosystems.

Limitations and known issues

Which major limitations should admins and users know?

Documented limitations include:

  • No mobile Hub experience
  • No version history in Hubs
  • No Shield Information Barriers support
  • No editable shared link to a Hub
  • Curated-content design rather than root-folder storage
  • Instant Login does not work with externally collaborated Hubs owned in another enterprise
  • External collaborators must be invited by main email address, not alias
  • Hub collaborations do not appear in the Admin Console External Users tab
How do user or enterprise migrations affect Hubs?

User content migrations can make the files or folders in a Hub unavailable. Enterprise migrations make all Hubs unavailable.

Troubleshooting

Why can a user not see Hubs in the left navigation?

Confirm that Box Hubs is enabled for the user or group, that navigation visibility includes managed users or creators as intended, and that the user is signing in on the web app rather than a mobile client.

Why can a user view a Hub by URL but not in the gallery?

An external collaborator whose own enterprise does not have Hubs enabled can open the Hub from its URL but not from their gallery.

Why is Make a Copy missing or greyed out?

Copy permission may be set to No one, limited to the enterprise, or locked by an admin. Contact the Hub co-owner or Box admin.

Why can an Editor not create a shared link or embed?

Hub settings may allow only co-owners to create or modify shared links. Enterprise shared-link settings may also block Hub links. Only Editors and Co-owners can create embeds; Viewers cannot.

Why did an embedded Hub fail to load?

Confirm the viewer has Hub access, the Hub is shared appropriately, third-party cookies are allowed, and the page is not a mobile-optimized experience that relies on the Embed Widget.

Box Hubs Known Issues and Limitations

Known Issues

Important

As of now, you can only invite users who have a Box account (any plan) to collaborate on a Hub.

User and enterprise migrations

Migrations have a negative impact on all Hubs created in the enterprise:

  • When a user migrates their content, the files and/or folders in a Hub become unavailable.
  • Enterprise migrations make all Hubs unavailable.

Limitations

  • Shield’s Information Barriers are not supported in Hubs.
  • Version history is not available.
  • As of now, Box Hubs does not work on mobile.
  • There is no current file or folder limit for a Hub. However, Box Hubs is meant to have curated content, not to serve as a location for root folders.
  • Hubs does not support an editable shared link to a Hub.
  • Instant Login (admin only feature) doesn’t work with externally collaborated hubs. An admin can’t use instant login for a user in their enterprise and view content owned in another enterprise’s hub.
  • As of now, you can only add external collaborators using their main email address. Using an email alias results in an error We were unable to add [xyz] as a collaborator.
  • Hub collaborations are not shown in the External Users tab in the Users & Groups section of Admin Console.
Box Hubs Limits

Restrictions for Box Hubs:

  • Number of Hubs for each tenant - no limits.
  • Number of Hubs for each Hub owner - no limits.
  • Number of collaborators for each Hub - existing Box limits apply for number of collaborations for each item.
  • Number of collaborations for each Hub - limited to 500. Group collaboration counts as 1, the group members are not counted.
  • Number of members for each group that can be added to or deleted from Hubs’ collaborators list - existing Box limits apply.
  • Number of paragraph sections in a Hub - no limit. <90 sections in a single Hub allows for an optimal viewing performance.
  • Number of files for Box AI for Hubs in a Hub - 20,000.
    • When the limit is reached, Box AI for Hubs responds with the following error message: You have exceeded the limit of 20,000 items for this Hub. Box AI is now disabled. To reenable Box AI, remove enough items to get below this limit.
  • Number of files for Box AI for Hubs across all the Hubs in an enterprise - 10,000,000. Note

When either of the limits for Box AI for Hubs are reached, the AI service responds with an error message.

Only the first 4 MB of a document is indexed by AI.

Box Hubs Permissions

There are four levels of permissions in Box Hubs: Admin, Co-Owner, Editor, and Viewer.

  • Admin can only enable Box Hubs for specific users/user groups.
  • Co-Owner has the broadest permissions.
  • Editor has the same permissions as a Co-Owner, except for creating and deleting a Hub, and managing Hub settings.
  • Viewer can’t make any changes to the Hubs they are invited to. Below table lists all actions each of them can perform in Hubs.

  • If a folder Uploader is invited to a Hub as Viewer, the folder Uploader permissions to the content change to Viewer/Uploader.

Box Hubs Reports

Box Hubs admin reports display the details of the Hubs in your enterprise. Reports are exported as .csv files to your Box Reports folder when complete.

Note

To run a report, you need to be an admin or have the requisite co-admin permissions.

Apart from running a report, you can save its configuration, schedule it, and subscribe specific users to it.

Box Hubs report details

  • File format: comma-separated value (.csv) file
  • Filename format: hubs_run_on_YYYY-MM-DD-HH-MM-SS_[A|P].csv

Box Hubs report columns

In the generated Box Hubs report you can find the following columns:

Hub ID

A unique identifier for the hub.

Hub Name

The name given to the Hub.

Hub Description

Any description entered when creating or editing the Hub. Will be blank if no description has been added.

Creator ID

A unique identifier ascribed to the person who created the Hub.

Creator’s User Name

The username of the individual who created the Hub.

Creator’s Email

The value in the Email field in User Account Details of the individual who created the Hub.

Created Date

The date that the Hub was created.

Number Of Total Views

The total number of times the Hub has been viewed, including repeat views.

Last Viewed

The date that the Hub was last viewed by any user.

Last Updated

The date that the Hub was last updated by any user.

Configuring Box Hubs

As a Box Admin, you can enable or disable Box Hubs for all your managed or selected users and groups.

  • Go to Admin Console > Enterprise Settings.
  • Select the Content and Sharing tab and scroll down to the Hubs section.
  • Select Configure.
  • Select one of the following settings:
    • Disable for all Hubs users
    • Enable for all Hubs users (recommended): on by default when you first log in to Box
    • Enable for select users or groups
    • Enable for everyone except select users or groups
    • See Enterprise Settings: Content & Sharing Tab for details.
    • Notes
      • These default settings only apply to Box accounts created as of November 4, 2025. Existing accounts retain their previous settings.
      • Enabling Box Hubs for specific users has the following limitations: You can enter up to 100 names/email addresses and up to 100 groups. If you want to enable or disable more, you must enable or disable Hubs for the entire organization.
  • Choose the visibility settings of Hubs in the navigation menu. Available options are:
    • Only users with permission to create Hubs.
    • All managed users (recommended).
  • Save your changes. Note

If you choose to disable Hubs creation but already have existing Hubs, contact our Support team to disable the product for your entire enterprise. If you disable Hubs creation in the Admin console, your users will still be able to view the Hubs gallery.

Setting up the default Hubs settings

You can set up some of Hubs’ behavior on an enterprise level.

Setting up the Shared Links section
  • Access the Admin Console.
  • Navigate to Enterprise Settings.
  • Go to the Content and Sharing tab.
  • Configure the Shared Links section:
    • Change Allow shared links for to either:
      • Folder, files, and hubs.
      • Folders only.
      • Files only.
      • Nothing, restrict sharing.
Setting up Collaborating on Content
  • Go to Admin Console > Enterprise Settings.
  • Scroll to the Collaborating on content section and limit the external collaboration by choosing one of the following options:
    • Enable external collaboration
    • Limit collaboration to allowlisted domains Note

This setting is global for all collaborated content, not only Hubs.

  • Scroll down to the Hubs section (if enabled).
  • Under Manage Hubs Global Presets option, click Edit Configuration to set the default Hub settings.
  • Configure the Who can access Hubs section:
    • Turn on Restrict collaboration to within [organization] to limit access to users in your organization.
      • Select Allow hub co-owners to change this setting to allow per-hub changes.
    • Turn on Restrict public shared links to block the creation of public shared links for Hubs.
      • Select Allow hub co-owners to change this setting to allow per-hub changes.
  • Configure who can copy Hubs:
    • Under Who can copy this Hub, select one of the following options:
      • No one
      • Only users within [organization]
      • Anyone
    • Select Allow hub co-owners to change this setting to allow per-hub changes.
  • Configure who can manage collaborators:
    • Under Who can add or modify collaborators, select one of the following options:
      • Editors and co-owners
      • Only co-owners
    • Select Allow hub co-owners to change this setting to allow per-hub changes.
  • Configure who can manage shared links:
    • Under Who can create or modify shared links, select one of the following options:
      • Editors and co-owners
      • Only co-owners
    • Select Allow hub co-owners to change this setting to allow per-hub changes.
  • Select Save to apply your changes.

Setting link expiration

You can set up shared links expiration for your enterprise. To do so:

  • Go to Admin Console > Enterprise Settings.
  • Select the Content & Sharing tab.
  • Scroll to the Auto-Expiration section.
  • Click the checkbox to select desired settings in Shared link expiration settings:
    • Disable all shared links after a specified time of link creation.
    • Disable public shared links after a specified time of link creation.
    • Apply these settings to - choose one:
      • Folders, files, and hubs
      • Folders and files
      • Folders only
      • Files only
      • Hubs only
    • Notify item owners a specified time before expiration
    • Allow item owners and editors to modify the expiration date
  • Save your changes. tech_writers_swarm_kb

Copying a Hub

You can copy an existing Hub to create a new one with the same structure and content. This is useful when you want to reuse a Hub layout without building it from scratch — for example, to create a similar knowledge base for a different team or project.

Note

Whether you can copy a Hub depends on the copy permission set by the Hub co-owner and your organization’s admin. If the copy option is not available, contact your Hub co-owner or admin.

What gets copied

When you copy a Hub, the following elements are included:

  • Hub name and description

  • Pages and page hierarchy

  • Logo and background image

  • Text blocks (paragraphs, section headers, callouts)

  • Embeds (link previews)

  • Dividers The following elements are not included in the copy:

  • Collaborators

  • Hub settings (copy permissions, collaboration restrictions, shared link settings) Files and folders are optional. When you initiate the copy, you can choose whether to include them. Only files and folders where you have Editor, Owner, or Co-owner access are copied. If your admin has enabled the Restrict invites setting for your enterprise, only content owners and co-owners can copy files with the Hub.

Note

File and folder blocks are always retained in the copied Hub structure, even when files are not copied. Blocks for files or folders that were not copied appear empty.

Copying a Hub

To copy a Hub:

  • Open the Hub you want to copy.
  • Click the ellipsis (…) > Make a Copy. The Copy “[Hub name]” Hub dialog opens.
  • In the Name Hub field, enter a name for the new Hub.
  • To include files and folders in the copy, select the Include files and folders checkbox.
  • Select Copy Hub. After the copy completes, you are automatically redirected to the new Hub.

Copying a Hub from another enterprise

If a Hub co-owner has enabled copying for external users, you can copy a Hub that belongs to a different organization. The copy is created in your own Box tenant and contains the same structure, pages, logo, background image, text blocks, and embeds as the original Hub.

Files and folders cannot be copied across enterprises. The Include files and folders checkbox is not available when copying a Hub from another organization. File and folder blocks are still retained in the copied Hub structure but appear empty.

Managing who can copy your Hub

As a Hub co-owner, you can control whether other users are allowed to copy your Hub.

To configure copy permissions:

  • Open the Hub.
  • Click the ellipsis (…) > View Settings.
  • Under Who can copy this hub, select one of the following options:
    • No one: Nobody can copy this Hub.
    • Only users within [your enterprise]: Only users in your enterprise can copy this Hub.
    • Anyone: All users with access to the Hub can copy it. Your organization’s admin can set organization-wide defaults for Hubs copy permissions and lock the setting to prevent co-owners from changing it. If the copy setting is greyed out, contact your admin.

Creating and Deleting a Hub

Create or delete a Hub in your enterprise and configure restrictions for your Hub.

  • Creating new Hub
  • Logo and background image
  • Co-owner settings on a Hub level
  • Embedding a Hub
  • Deleting a Hub

Creating new Hub

To create a Hub:

  • Do one of the following:

    • In the sidebar, click the plus icon next to Hubs. The Hub creation page opens in a new tab.
    • In the Hubs gallery, click the New Hub button. If this is your first Hub, you see a You don’t have any Hubs yet message with a step-by-step tutorial. Click Get Started.

  • Fill in the Hub name and description.

  • Add any files that you want. Refer to Adding Content to Box Hubs for more information.

  • Save your changes. Restrictions

  • If you don’t specify a Hub name, it is auto-populated with Untitled Hub [date and time].

  • If you don’t add any description, it is not auto-populated and is not visible on the published Hub.

  • A Hub description can only have 2000 characters.

  • You can only add files or folders owned by your enterprise to your Hub. You can change both the name and description in the edit mode.

Logo and background image

You can add a logo and background images when you create your Hub, or later in the edit mode. You can center-align the logo. Doing so also center-aligns the hub name and description. For details, see Working with the Box Hubs Builder.

To add a logo or background image, click the pencil icon on the logo or background. Then select an image from the gallery or upload it from Box or from your device.

To delete a custom image, you need to first change the custom logo or background to another one. Then you need to click the pencil icon to open the gallery. Find your image in the gallery and click the X button on it. A pop-up message appears, asking you to confirm the image deletion.

Important

If you delete the custom image, you won’t be able to restore it, but you can add it again from Box or from your device.

For the logo, we recommend using a square image. For the background, we recommend choosing images with a 5:1 aspect ratio and minimum width of 1600 px.

Note

Only images in jpg or png format and smaller than 5 MB are accepted.

Co-owner settings on a Hub level

As a co-owner you can edit the Hub settings both in the edit and view mode. To do so:

  • Open the desired Hub.
  • Click the ellipsis to open the More Options menu.
  • Click Hub Settings. Important

Your Hubs admin can change the default Hubs options for your enterprise. Depending on that, some of the below options can be greyed out. Contact your Hubs admin for more information.

The following options are available:

  • Restrict collaboration to within your enterprise: on by default when you first log in to Box. To allow adding external collaborators, turn this option off.
  • Control who can copy this Hub:
    • No one: the Make a Copy option is hidden for all users.
    • Only users within [your enterprise]: only internal users can copy. External users, including those with a shared link, cannot see the copy option.
    • Anyone (default): all users with access, including external collaborators and shared link users, can copy.
  • Control who can add or modify the collaborators:
    • Editors and co-owners (on by default when you first log in to Box)
    • Only co-owners
  • Control who can create or modify shared links:
    • Editors and co-owners (on by default when you first log in to Box)
    • Only co-owners
  • Manage Box AI features for this Hub. Note

These default settings only apply to Box accounts created as of November 4, 2025. Existing accounts retain their previous settings.

Note

You can’t enable shared links in Hub settings if:

  • You’re an admin and you disabled shared links in the admin console for your enterprise.
  • You’re a Hub editor, but the Hub co-owner didn’t give you permissions to do that. Permissions should be set to Invited People Only, and you can configure the other settings.

Embedding a Hub

Only Hub editors and co-owners can create an embedded widget for a Hub. Viewers cannot create shared links or embeds for Hubs they have access to.

To embed a Hub anywhere on your webpage or system:

  • Open the Hub you want to embed.
  • Click the ellipsis to open the More Options menu.
  • Click Embed Hub.
  • Select the size of the widget. Available options are:
    • Small (330 x 400),
    • Medium (500 x 400),
    • Large (800 x 550),
    • Custom.
  • Copy the link and add it in the desired place. Check the Hide Hubs Gallery option to prevent users from going to the Hubs Gallery in the widget.

Note

To see the contents of the embedded Hub, you need to be invited to it or have access through the shared link. You must be a Hub editor or co-owner to create the embed or the shared link for the Hub.

Deleting a Hub

To delete a Hub:

  • Select the specific Hub from the Hub gallery.
  • Click the More options menu.
  • Select Delete Hub. A pop-up message with the following information appears:

Are you sure you want to delete this Hub? The Hub will be deleted and users will lose access to some or all files in this Hub.

Confirm the Hub deletion by ticking the I acknowledge this action cannot be undone checkmark in the pop-up message.

Note

You must be a Hub Co-Owner to delete a Hub. When you delete it, the source content from Box is not deleted.

Hubs Admin Management

As a Box admin or co-admin you can manage and access all Hubs from your enterprise within the Admin Console.

Managing Hubs in your enterprise

Open the Admin Console, go to Content → Hubs tab, where you can see a table with all Hubs in your organization, with the following columns:

  • Hub Name
  • Created By
  • Number of Views
  • Last Viewed
  • Date Updated
  • Co-Owners
  • Collaborators Note

When you hover over a name in the Created By column, the name and email address of the creator appear in an info box. If there is an icon next to the creator’s name, hover over the icon to see more information.

From the list view you can:

  • Manage shared links.
  • Search for Hubs by name or Hub ID in the search bar.
  • Delete a Hub.
  • Filter and sort specific fields.
  • Change Hub settings.
  • Set permissions for Co-Admins. The available options are:
    • View Hubs for your company
    • Manage, share, and delete Hubs for your company To sort the listed Hubs, click on the column name, for example Hub Name.

Click the ellipsis (…) next to a Hub to open the context menu with the following options:

  • Share Hub - opens the standard sharing modal.
  • Manage Collaborators - click Share → Shared with. You can add collaborators in the new modal.
  • Hub Settings - opens specific Hubs’ settings.
  • Delete Hub - opens the standard deleting modal. You can also filter the listed Hubs by using quick filters: click Number of Views or Date Updated button, or choose other filtering parameters after clicking the Filters button.

Note

You can also access Hub settings by going to the Hubs tab on the Content and Sharing page in Admin console. Review any pop-up messages and save the changes you made. As a Hub admin or co-admin with managing permissions here you can manage the specific Hub settings that are locked from your Hub co-owners.

Searching Box Hubs

Search Box Hubs in the Hubs gallery or inside a Hub. Use filters to make your search more detailed.

Note

In the edit mode, click the Select Metadata to add filters that allow your users to search for content faster.

Hubs gallery

To search for a specific Hub, go to the Hubs gallery and enter the Hub name in the search bar.

You can also filter and sort the Hubs.

Filter options:
  • All
  • View Access
  • Edit Access
Sort options:
  • Recently updated
  • Most viewed Note

Search indexes only the first 200 characters of a Hub description. This is the same text that appears on the Hub card in the Hubs gallery. Content beyond the first 200 characters isn’t indexed and won’t appear in search results.

Inside a Hub

Open the Hub and enter a keyword in the Hub search bar. You can also click the Filters icon in the search bar and use filters to make your search results more specific.

You can filter the content by:

  • File Type (multi-choice)
    • Document
    • PDF
    • Presentation
    • Spreadsheet
    • Image
    • Video
    • Audio
    • Drawing
    • 3D
    • Box Note
    • Box Canvas
  • Date Updated (multi-choice)
    • Any time
    • Last day
    • Last week
    • Last month
    • Last year
    • Custom range (you need to specify the date range)
  • Owners (type in the name of the owner)
  • Metadata On the search results page, you can sort the files by their relevance and update date (newest or oldest).

Note

You can also use the global search, the Hub files are included in the search results.

Metadata

To add metadata to your Hub search, click the Select Metadata button.

Select the metadata filter from the dropdown list under the Metadata section, for example Background Check Alert.

tech_writers_swarm_kb

Sharing a Hub

  • Sharing with groups
  • Sharing using a shared link
    • Shared link settings
    • Setting a shared link expiration date
  • Restricting public shared links
  • Removing collaborators You can share your Hub like any other Box content. You can select only one of the two permission levels: Viewer or Editor, or make a user a Co-Owner of the Hub.

Important

Granting a user access to a Hub automatically gives them Viewer permissions to all files and folders in that Hub. This does not apply to external or Box links embedded in the Hub using Link Preview.

You can also generate a public link to share a Hub with both Box users and people without a Box account.

Note

  • By default, you cannot invite external users to collaborate on a Hub. To enable external collaboration, turn off this restriction in your Hub settings. See Co-owner settings on the Hub level for details.
  • External users can only be viewers and must have an existing Box account.

Sharing with groups

Only groups with permissions other than Admins Only show up on the list of groups you can share a Hub with. Admins can still add Admins Only groups to a Hub, but only through the Admin Console > Content > Hubs.

Make sure you have the necessary permissions to add the group. For details, see Creating and Managing Groups.

Sharing using a shared link

Only Hub editors and co-owners can create a shared link for a Hub to send it to people from the enterprise and outside of it. Viewers cannot create shared links for Hubs.

Both the internal and external users have to sign in to Box to access the content of a Hub, unless you chose the permission level People with the link.

Note

If you access Box Hubs through a shared link and you have an editor access to some files or folders, you can’t edit them from a Hub level. For more information on shared links see Creating Shared Links.

Shared link settings

As a Hub editor, you can configure the shared link options. For more information, see Configuring Individual Shared Link Settings.

Note

If you have the Viewer permissions, you can check what settings are in place for a specific shared link to learn what you can do with it.

To enable the chosen setting, tick the checkbox under the option. The available options are:

  • Link Expiration - Set an expiration date for your shared link
  • Password Protect - Require password
  • Non-private custom URL - Publish content broadly with a custom, non-private URL
  • Allow Download - Allow users with the shared link to download this item Note

If there is a Shield policy in place that restricts downloads, the Download button is visible only in Preview.

Setting a shared link expiration date

As a Hub co-owner or editor you can setup an expiration date for a shared link. To do so:

  • Open the shared link settings.
  • Click Disable Shared Link on under Link Expiration.
  • Select the expiration date. When you set the expiration date for a link, you can see a red clock icon next to the information Shared link is created. When you hover over the icon, a message This link will expire and be inaccessible on [date].

Changing an existing expiration date

To change the existing expiration date:

  • Open the shared link settings.
  • Click the Choose Date input field or the calendar icon.
  • Choose the new link expiration date and save the settings. Disabling an existing link expiration

To disable link expiration:

  • Open the shared link settings.
  • Uncheck the checkbox Disable Shared Link on under Link Expiration.
  • Save your changes. The red clock icon disappears.

Note

Your enterprise admin can enable link expirations on an enterprise level. When you are a Hub co-owner or editor, you can change the expiration date in the link settings.

Restricting public shared links

As a Hub co-owner, you can prevent your Hub from being shared publicly through Anyone with the link. This reduces the risk of accidental oversharing while still allowing intentional exceptions where needed.

Note

Your enterprise admin can set a global default for this setting. If the admin has locked this setting, you won’t be able to change it at the individual Hub level.

To restrict public shared links for a Hub:

  • Open the Hub you want to configure.
  • Click the ellipsis (…) > View Settings.
  • In the Who can access this Hub section, turn on the Restrict public shared links toggle.
  • Save your changes. When this setting is enabled, users will only be able to share the Hub with people within your organization or specific individuals, not with Anyone with the link.

Note

The Restrict public shared links setting applies only to new Hubs and is not retroactive to existing Hubs. If your Hub was created before your admin enabled this setting, and your Hub already has a public shared link (Anyone with the link), you may see a configuration conflict error message in Hub Settings.

Removing collaborators

To remove collaborators from a Hub:

  • Click the Share button.
  • Click Shared with.
  • Click Manage All.
  • Choose Remove from the drop-down list.

Troubleshooting Box Hubs - Unable to Add Folders

Overview of Problem

Users with Editor access on a folder may find that they are unable to add the folder to a Box Hub. This issue occurs when the folder has a specific collaboration restriction enabled, preventing Editors from adding the folder to a Hub. This affects the ability to manage and organize content within Box Hubs.

Process for Resolution

  • Verify User Role on the Folder
    • Confirm the user’s collaboration role on the folder (Owner, Co-owner, Editor).
  • Check Folder Collaboration Restrictions
    • Open the folder in Box.
    • Click Folder settings → go to Collaboration → Invitation Restrictions.
    • Look for the checkbox labeled: Only folder owners and co-owners can send collaborator invites and add this folder to a Hub.
      • If the checkbox is enabled (checked), only the folder Owner or Co-owner can add the folder to a Hub — Editors cannot.
      • If the checkbox is disabled (unchecked), Editors (and other permitted roles) that meet the Hub’s requirements can add the folder.
  • Remedial Actions (if change is desired)
    • If you want Editors to be able to add the folder to a Hub, have an Owner or Co-owner open Folder settings and uncheck the invitation restriction.
    • Alternatively, have an Owner or Co-owner add the folder to the Hub on behalf of the Editor.

Outcome

  • Users with Editor access on a folder should be able to successfully add the folder to the hub.

Alternatives

  • Workaround: Elevate Editor users to Co-owner for the affected folders to enable adding to Hubs.
  • Permanent Remediation: Disable the folder restriction on the relevant folders (or on the parent folder if the setting should apply to all descendants and is inherited).
  • Bulk Updates: For large numbers of folders, perform bulk updates programmatically (Box API) or plan scripted automation.
  • Escalation: If you continue to experience any of the symptoms listed above, collect a HAR network capture while reproducing the error, then open a support ticket at support.box.com for further assistance.

Further Reading

  • Adding Content to Box Hubs
  • Box API Reference

Working with the Box Hubs Builder

The Box Hubs builder provides an intuitive interface for organizing your Hub content. The builder uses the same interaction model as other Box tools, making it easy to learn and use.

  • Before you begin
  • Edit your Hub
  • Content blocks
  • Sections
  • Pages
  • Notify collaborators of changes

Before you begin

To organize a Hub, you must have co-owner or editor permissions. For details, see Box Hubs Permissions.

Edit your Hub

To open a Hub in edit mode:

  • Go to the Hubs gallery.
  • Select the Hub you want to edit.
  • In the upper-right corner, select Edit. The Add Block panel appears on the right side. The panel displays all available content block types you can add to your Hub.

Logo and header alignment

You can center-align the logo in the Hub builder. When you center-align the logo, the hub name and description are also center-aligned.

Content blocks

Content blocks are the building blocks of your Hub. Each block type serves a different purpose:

Block type

Description

Files and Folders

Add content from your Box account.

Section Header

Create an organizational section with a title (up to 100 characters).

Paragraph

Add text content (up to 5000 characters).

Link Cards

Add a block that displays a set of cards, each linking to a configurable destination.

Call Out

Highlight important information in a new call out window (up to 5000 characters).

Link Preview

Embed interactive content directly in your Hub.

Divider

Add a visual separator between content.

Add a block

Use either method to add a block:

Method 1: Click to add

  • In the Add Block panel, select the block type.

  • The block appears at the end of the page. Method 2: Drag to add

  • In the Add Block panel, drag the block type onto the page.

  • Drop it in the desired location.

Manage blocks

To manage a block:

  • Select the block on the canvas.
  • The context toolbar appears with available options:
    • Move up or down
    • Move to a Different Page
    • Duplicate
    • Trash
    • Add Items (for Files and Folders blocks)
    • Display as grid or list (for Files and Folders blocks)
    • Formatting toolbar (for Paragraph and Call Out blocks) To reposition a block, select it and drag it to the new location.

Note

In Files and Folders blocks, individual files become draggable only after you select the block. This prevents accidental movement.

  • List view: Drag and drop files or folders to reorder them.
  • Grid view: Select a file or folder, click the … (three dots) at the bottom of the card, and click the Move Left or Move Right arrow.
Delete a block
  • Select the block.
  • On the context toolbar, select Trash.
Link Cards

The Link Cards block displays a row of customizable cards that link to Hub pages, Box content, or external URLs. When you add the block, three empty cards appear by default.

To configure a card, select it, add a link, and edit the title, description, or background image. When you add a link, the card pulls the title, description, and image from the destination if those details are available. Cards that link outside your enterprise show an external link icon and open in a new tab.

To manage cards within the block:

  • Select Add Card to add a card.
  • Select Trash on the card toolbar to remove a card.
  • Use the arrows on the card toolbar to reorder cards. From the block’s context toolbar, switch between Left Align (default) and Fill (full-width) layouts.

Notes

  • A Link Cards block must contain at least one card. When you remove the last card, the entire block is deleted from the page.
  • If you save the Hub with a card that has no link added, that card isn’t shown when viewers open the Hub. Important

Hub access doesn’t automatically grant viewers access to the destination of a card. If a viewer doesn’t have access, they see the standard error state on the destination page.

Sections

Sections help you organize related content by creating visual separators on your page. Each section title marks the beginning of a new section.

Create a section
  • In the Add Block panel, select Section Title or drag it onto the page.
  • Enter a section title (up to 100 characters).
  • Add content blocks to your section. When you add a section title, an outline is created automatically in the Hub navigation. This makes browsing easier for viewers.
Reorder sections
  • Select the section title.
  • In the context toolbar, select Move Up or Move Down.
  • Move the section to the desired position.
Rename a section
  • Select the section title.
  • Enter the new title.
Delete a section
  • Select the section.
  • In the context toolbar, select Trash.

Pages

Pages provide another level of organization in your Hub. You can create multiple pages and nest them to build a clear hierarchy.

Add a page
  • In the Hub Outline panel, select Add Page (+).
  • Replace the default title with your page name. The default title format is “Untitled Page [yyyy-mm-dd hh:mm:ss].”
Add a nested page

Nested pages (subpages) appear under a parent page in the hierarchy.

  • In the Hub Outline panel, hover over the parent page.
  • Select the ellipsis (…) to open the page options.
  • Select Add Nested Page.
  • Enter a title for the nested page.
Duplicate a page
  • In the Hub Outline panel, hover over the page.
  • Select the ellipsis (…) to open the page options.
  • Select Duplicate Page.
Change page hierarchy

You can reorganize your pages at any time:

  • Reorder pages: Drag a page up or down to change its position.
  • Create nested pages: Drag a page onto another page to make it a subpage.
  • Promote nested pages: Drag a subpage into the main page area to make it a top-level page. Note

Your home page is always the highest page in the hierarchy and can’t be moved.

Delete a page
  • In the Hub Outline panel, hover over the page.
  • Select the ellipsis (…) to open the page options.
  • Select Delete Page.
  • In the confirmation dialog, select Delete. Important

When you delete a page, all content within it is deleted, including blocks and nested pages. This action can’t be reversed.

Notify collaborators of changes

After you make changes to your Hub, you can notify all collaborators through email.

Send a change notification
  • Make your changes to the Hub.
  • In the upper-right corner, select Save > Save & Notify Collaborators.
  • In the notification dialog, enter a message describing your changes.
  • Select Save & Notify. All Hub collaborators receive an email notification with your custom message and a link to open the Hub. As the sender, you do not receive this email notification.
Save without notifying

If you don’t want to notify collaborators:

  • Make your changes to the Hub.
  • In the upper-right corner, select Save. Your changes are saved, but collaborators don’t receive an email notification.

Box Mobile

Accessing Content Using Document Provider

  • Overview
  • Document Picker Security Settings
  • The Microsoft Excel Example
  • Behavior

Overview

Apple’s Document Provider extension allows third-party applications to open files from Box (or any cloud storage provider) and save them back to Box without any special integrations within Box. Once you install the Box app on the iOS device, Box shows up as a Document Provider in the Apple UI.

The Document Provider extension allows third-party Box apps (for example, Microsoft Excel) to access documents managed by Box.

The Document Provider consists of two view controllers:

  • Document Picker: Displays the Apple user interface when third-party users access a Box document. In this article, we refer to Box as the Document Provider. The third-party app invokes the Document Picker.
  • File Provider: Allows third-party users to select, preview, download, or upload Box documents.

Document Picker Security Settings

The Content can be opened in external applications setting allows Admins to control the user’s ability to open content from Box in other applications from the same device. See Mobile Security Settings for more information.

The Files can be opened in applications that save back to Box (iOS only) setting allows the document picker to open files from Box in external applications and save changes back to Box.

Note: The iOS Document Provider functionality does not alert providers (for example, Box) about which app is making the request. As a result, Box does not currently have a way to provide an allow list (the ability for an Admin to sanction which apps are allowed to access files on Box ﹣ like Document Provider).

Currently, an Admin cannot restrict users to Box as a Document Provider with only iAnnotate and block other third-party apps. Box allows all apps or none at all.

The Microsoft Excel Example

Following up on the Microsoft Excel example, here is the process when an Excel user opens a file using Box:

  • The users verify that their admin has enabled the Open files in external applications settings. If the Admin has disabled these settings (and, consequently, Document Provider), users will not be able to access their Box files from the Document Picker window.
  • When Box third-party users open a file, they are presented with options. The options include cloud providers who have their applications installed on the device and who have implemented Document Provider. To open a Box file in Excel, users click Open (1), Locations (2), and then select Box (3). (To add Box as a Content Provider in Microsoft Office apps, see: To set up Box as a Content Provider).
  • When Excel users select Box, iOS displays the Document Picker window with the Box Document Picker UI. Excel users can navigate their folders in Box from this view and select and open the file.
  • When users are done editing or viewing the document, they can save the file back to Box from Excel.

Behavior

When using Box via the iOS Document Picker, be aware of the following behavioral nuances:

  • The iOS Document Picker UI present you with the Login Screen if you’re logged out of the Box app. SSO works in this scenario ﹣ if you log in using Document Picker, you are also logged into Box.
  • We currently do not offer offline support in the Document Picker. You must be connected to the internet to make use of this feature. tech_writers_swarm_kb

Annotating a PDF With Notability

Notability allows users to create, edit, and share business plans all in one place. Both beautiful and functional, Notability seamlessly combines three major ways to capture information: handwriting, typing, and recording. It contains a powerful feature set that helps you be more productive, and provides the tools to capture, create, and share information more effectively.

There are two ways Box uniquely integrates with Notability.

First, you can start notes in Notability and then send them to Box. Simply tap share in Notability, select Box, and pick your destination folder. Furthermore, if you set up auto-sync in Notability, all of your notes will automatically be sent to Box without you having to think about it.

Second, you can start notes in Box or edit documents you receive from coworkers. To start a note in Box, tap the cloud in the lower-left-hand corner and select Notability. Then when you’re done, tap the Box arrow and your file will be saved to Box. Additionally, if you receive PDFs, RTFs, or Notes from coworkers, these can be opened and edited in Notability. Tap the document to view it in Box, then tap the cloud in the upper-right-hand corner, and select Edit in Notability. Once you’re done, tap the Box arrow and you’ll be taken right back to Box.

If you have SSO, you can log into Box through Notability by entering your email address and leaving the password blank. You will then be redirected to your active directory page where you can login using your company credentials.

You can download Notability here and if you experience any issues, you can reach Notability support at support@gingerlabs.com.

Annotating PDFs in iAnnotate

With iAnnotate PDF, anyone can manage, store, and annotate hundreds of PDF files on their iPad. From the shortest contracts to the lengthiest journals, iAnnotate’s scrolling page view and customizable annotation tools, allows you to mark up documents with ease and flexibility. You can open numerous PDFs at once, create a toolbar of your favorite highlighter colors, drag and drop files in the library, all this and many more features you’ll find only in iAnnotate PDF.

Linking iAnnotate to your Box account

It’s easy to link iAnnotate PDF to one or more of your Box accounts.

  1. Within iAnnotate tap on Library (located in the upper left hand corner) and then tap on Connections.

  2. Tap Add Box and enter a description (it defaults to Box). Enter your Box username, typically your email address and choose Read Only if you want to use the connection to import files, but wish to disable syncing annotated files back to your Box account. With this option turned on, your annotations will only be saved to your iPad and not backed up to Box. When you are finished tap on Set Up Connection.

  3. You will find the new Box connection icon in your Library; it will appear light gray meaning you have not downloaded anything from it yet. Tap the icon to continue the setup process.

  4. Your username will already be entered (if you’ve made a mistake and mistyped this you will need to delete this connection and make a new one since you cannot edit the username in the authorization window). If your username is not already entered, just input this, along with your password and tap on ‘Authorize’.

  5. You will then be asked to let iAnnotate grant access to Box. Tap Grant access to Box.

  6. Once setup is complete, you will see all of your folders within your Box account displayed in iAnnotate.

  7. After you download your first file from Box into iAnnotate, your Box connection icon will no longer be displayed in light gray.

  8. To remove your Box connection, simply tap and hold down the Box connection icon and click on Delete.

Annotating PDF’s in iAnnotate

Once your Box account is set up, you can manage your PDF documents with a range of commands: download documents and directories of PDFs from Box to iAnnotate, quickly upload any annotated or modified PDFs back to Box, or even upload new documents to your Box account.

  1. In iAnnotate navigate and open your PDF document that you would like to edit.

  2. You will see a toolbar on the right hand side your your screen. This toolbar is limited to 12 tools and can be customized by tapping on the ‘+’ icon at the top of the toolbar, which will automatically open the toolbox.

There are a number of different tools that you can use in order to annotate a PDF document. Some tools include highlighting text, leaving notes, underlining text, adding images, signatures or stamps etc. They are just some of the many tools that are available for you to use in order to annotate a PDF file.

  1. To Highlight text, tap on the highlight icon and highlight the text.

  2. Then tap on the ‘tick’ icon to save this. If you wish to remove the highlight, just tap on the highlighted text and then tap on the Trash icon.

  3. To leave a Note within the PDF document, just tap on the note icon, enter your note and then tap on the ‘tick’ icon to save. If you wish to remove this note, tap on the note and then tap on the Trash icon.

Once you have finished annotating your PDF file you can save and upload these changes back to Box.

  1. Tap on the file at the top of your screen, click on Share and then Upload to Box as an annotated PDF. This PDF file will then get stored into the folder that we select, as a copy of the original PDF document.

You can download iAnnotate here and if you run into any issues with the app you can contact their support team at support@branchfire.com.

Annotating PDFs In PDF Expert

PDF Expert lets you read and annotate PDF documents, highlight text, make notes, draw with your finger and save these changes being compatible with Preview and Adobe Acrobat. Moreover, PDF Expert is the only iPad application that can fill PDF forms!

PDF Expert reads almost all document types like: iWork, MS Office, Power Point, text files, images, even music and video files, etc. It can retrieve documents from any place you may need. Application Administrators

Setting up Box for EMM

Work with Box Product Support to set up Box for EMM for your enterprise. For configuration of your EMM policies, contact your EMM provider.

Make sure you comply with the following requirements:

  • Box for EMM only works if your users got the app from your company’s EMM provider,
  • users must already have an EMM provider account,
  • users cannot download the EMM directly from a public app store. The app must be provisioned by the administrator,
  • users cannot back up the app from one device and restore it on another device. Apple’s Files app introduced in iOS 11 makes it possible to move or copy files from Box for EMM folders to other folders outside of Box’s environment. This means it’s possible to use your iOS device to make files accessible to people who should not have access to them, or to the general public. This behavior occurs only in versions older than iOS 12.1. For more information on supported versions, see Understand the Box Policy For Browser And OS Support.

Note:

To avoid these issues, update to version 12.1 or higher.

This behavior impacts only content stored on Box for enterprises that use Box for EMM in an MDM environment. If your enterprise does not use an MDM solution and Box for EMM on iOS, your data is not affected.

Important:

Since latest version of the apps won’t install on iOS 11, this is not a concern for most admins.

If your users need to use and older version of iOS, you prevent the behavior in the affected iOS versions. Navigate to Admin Console > Enterprise Settings > Mobile and turn on Disable iOS Files functionality on devices running iOS 12.0 or older (iOS EMM only). To learn more, see Using the iOS EMM Unprotected & Protected Checkbox.

Login error messages and causes

If your users are having trouble logging in, see the table below for possible causes:

Error Message

Possible Causes

Could not complete login because the app is not authorized. Please contact your administrator for more information.

  • The user installed Box for EMM from the public app store, instead of receiving it from their EMM provider.

  • The user backed up the app on one device and restored it on another device.

  • The device is out of compliance with its EMM provider. Could not complete login because the user is not authorized. Please contact your administrator for more information.

  • The user is not part of the enterprise that provisioned the app.

  • Incorrect managed app configs have been loaded onto the device. No message (returns user to the login screen)

  • Box for EMM was configured incorrectly during initial setup.

  • The device is not connected to the internet.

Moving enterprise from Box app to Box for EMM app

During the move, you can allow test users to use both the Box for EMM and standard Box apps. However, after completing the move, you must disable the Box for iPhone and iPad, or Box for Android apps, so users cannot log into their enterprise accounts through these apps.

To disable these apps for your enterprise, go to the Admin Console, navigate to Enterprise Settings > Apps. In the Official Box Applications section, select the apps you wish to disable.

Application Users

Downloading Box for EMM

To download Box for EMM (Enterprise Mobility Management), contact your administrator. Don’t download the application from the app store.

Note:

The above applies if your enterprise uses MDM (Mobile Device Management) only. If your company doesn’t use MDM, you can download the standard Box app (Box for mobile) from your app store.

Once Box for EMM is installed on your device, by default you can search for it in the app store to update. However, your admin may have disabled the manual update option. If that is so, contact your admin for updates.

Notifications

Box for EMM does not support push notifications on iOS.

On Android you can configure push notifications yourself.

The Box app can send notifications to you when someone:

  • invites you to collaborate on an item, and you have enabled auto-acceptance of collaborations,
  • comments on a file you own,
  • comments on a file you previously commented on,
  • @-mentions you on a file,
  • edits a file that is highly relevant to you, where Box determines relevance based on your history of accessing the file.

Box as a Managed Place in Microsoft Intune

Overview

Box and Microsoft have enabled a new capability for Intune Mobile Application Management (MAM aka App Protection Policy) that allows saving copies of org-managed documents to Box from the relevant Microsoft mobile apps (i.e. Office, Word, PowerPoint, Excel, and Outlook apps). Previously, enterprises that leveraged Intune MAM were limited to OneDrive and SharePoint as managed cloud storage providers. Box as a Managed Place in Intune now provides enterprises the option to control the flow of managed data to move between Microsoft and Box, and block any attempts to save copies of org-managed data outside of Box.

Supported Microsoft Mobile Apps

iOS: Office, Word, Powerpoint, Excel, Outlook

Android: Office, Word, Powerpoint, Excel

Technical Requirements

Enterprises will be required to have Azure Active Directory (AAD) or Okta federation for their Box login in order to utilize the Box as a Managed Place functionality in the relevant Microsoft mobile apps. Enterprises are not required to have a Mobile Device Management (MDM) solution to enable the functionality because the functionality is part of Microsoft’s Intune MAM policy aka app protection policy, meaning it’s available for both MDM enrolled devices and unenrolled devices.

Enable Box as a Managed Place from the Microsoft Intune Portal

To enable the Box as a Manage Place functionality, a Microsoft Intune admin at your enterprise must log into the Microsoft Endpoint Manager admin center and navigate to the relevant MAM policy aka app protection policy that is associated to their enterprise’s relevant Microsoft mobile apps.

From the MAM policy, click on the Edit button within the “Data protection” section of the policy and find the “Save copies of org data” policy setting. Select “Block” and then under the “Allow user to save copies to selected services” dropdown, select “Box”. This will block saving copies of org data outside of Box within the relevant Microsoft mobile apps associated to the MAM policy, i.e. saving copies of org data is allowed only within Box.

Notes:

  • If you can’t edit Office files in Box for EMM (for example after enabling the Office Co-Authoring feature), enable saving to Box in Intune in the app protection policy. To do so, select Box in Allow users to save copies to selected services. Check the Microsoft documentation to make sure that the setting name is up to date.
  • If users want to save files to Box (with co-authuring or not) and have an app protection policy that restricts the locations where content from Office is saved, users must enable saving to Box in Intune.

End Users Enabling Box as a Managed Place

End users will first need to install the latest version of the relevant Microsoft mobile apps. Once installed, a user should navigate to the Open tab (folder icon) and in the “Other Storage” section, select “Add Storage Account” and then select Box. Once the end user has successfully authorized Microsoft to access their Box account, they’re all set, and the relevant Intune MAM policies will be applied to the end user.
