Using the Box for iOS Security Settings

For our more security-oriented users, Box for iOS offers the ability to add an extra layer of security to our Box for iOS application. By default, after a user logs into the application, they can access their content by simply clicking back into the app. If you’d like to add extra protection, you can enable our App Passcode feature.

The App Passcode feature allows a user to set a 4-digit PIN that will pop up after a chosen amount of time away from the app. By default, this time limit is set to Immediately, which means closing the app and clicking right back in will trigger the PIN requirement.

Note: this functionality is separate from the iOS passcode presented at the Home Screen of your iOS device. That code allows access to your full phone, while the passcode mentioned in the article only controls access to the Box for iOS application.

Enabling the Box for iOS App Passcode

To enable the passcode, please follow the steps below:

  • Log in to the Box for iOS application.
  • Tap the Gear icon in the top-left corner to access Settings.
  • In the Settings, select Security.
  • Tap Turn Passcode On.
  • Choose a passcode and enter it on the number pad.
  • Confirm your passcode.
  • If you would like to change the time limit to prompt the Passcode, tap the Lock setting and choose the time setting you prefer.

Enabling TouchID or FaceID

Box also allows users to leverage the iOS functionality TouchID or FaceID once they have a passcode set. Here is how to enable this feature:

  • Once the passcode is set, return to the Security Option page.
  • Enable the TouchID/FaceID setting.
  • Complete the TouchID/FaceID prompt to confirm the setup. tech_writers_swarm_kb

Using the Box Notification Center on Mobile

The Box Notification Center on Mobile displays a summary of notifications sent to you by Box, and by the people you work with. Notifications can include

  • @mentions,
  • collaboration invitations,
  • shared link announcements,
  • file annotations,
  • task reminders, and
  • updates on collaborator activities. If you turn off auto-acceptance of incoming invitations, the Box Notification Center on Mobile enables you to accept or decline collaboration invitations. The Notification Center also displays invitations to enroll in two-factor authentication (2FA), accept Terms of Service, or set a strong password to access shared content.

With support on Android and iOS, the Box Notification Center enables you to review your workflow notifications on the go, so you can quickly and efficiently stay up-to-date on the work you’re involved in.

Note

  • Support on Android is coming soon for
    • task notifications,
    • accepting invitations to enroll in two-factor authentication (2FA),
    • accepting Terms of Service, and
    • accepting invitations to set a strong password.
  • The Notification Center does not provide expiration notifications, but Box does send these notifications to you through email.
  • The Notification Center does not support filtering of notifications.

Reviewing your notifications

When you receive a notification, Box displays a badge next to the Notification Center in your Inbox showing how many unread notifications you have.

To review your notifications:

  • In the footer bar, tap Inbox.

  • In the top of the Inbox window, a badge next to Notifications displays how many unread notifications you have. Tap Notifications.

  • Box displays the list of your notifications. Unread notifications have a blue background, and read notifications have a white background. To accept or decline an invitation:

  • In the footer bar, tap Inbox.

  • At the top of the Inbox window, tap Notifications.

  • Below the invitation, tap View Details.

  • In the invitation, tap Accept, or tap Decline. tech_writers_swarm_kb

Using the Box Task Center on Mobile

The Box Task Center on Mobile displays a summary of tasks assigned to you, a summary of tasks you assigned to other people, their due dates, and statuses. The Box Task Center also enables you to mark a task as completed, approved, or rejected.

With support on Android and iOS, the Box Task Center on Mobile enables you to review all your assigned tasks on the go, so you can quickly and efficiently review the status and due dates of the work you’re involved in.

To see tasks assigned to you:

  • In the footer bar, tap Inbox.

  • In the top of the Inbox window, a badge on MY TASKS displays how many unfinished tasks you have. Tap MY TASKS. To see the status of tasks you’ve assigned:

  • In the footer bar, tap Inbox.

  • In the top of the Inbox window, tap SENT TASKS. To resolve a task:

  • In the footer bar, tap Inbox.

  • In the top of the Inbox window, tap MY TASKS.

  • Below the task, tap

    • Mark as Complete, or
    • Approve, or
    • Reject. If you assigned a task to yourself, you can also resolve it through SENT TASKS.

Both MY TASKS and SENT TASKS show the 20 most recently assigned tasks.

Using the iOS EMM Unprotected & Protected Checkbox

Note

This article does not apply to you if:

  • Your version of iOS is greater than 12.1, in which case the content on your Managed Apps is protected.
  • Your enterprise does not use an MDM solution and Box for EMM on iOS. In iOS 11, Apple introduced the Files app to bring all your files together in one convenient place, and enable access on not only the Apple device, but also on other apps across cloud services.

The Files app enables you to access content through Box for Enterprise Mobility Management (EMM) in conjunction with a Mobile Device Management (MDM) system.

In the Edit menu of the Files app, Box discovered an unexpected behavior in the Move, Copy, and Share actions that allows content from Managed Apps to be passed to Unmanaged Apps.

This can occur even when the MDM configuration is set to disallow documents to be opened in Unmanaged Apps and accounts, for example in personal storage, iCloud, and so on.

As a workaround to this unexpected behavior, you can disable the iOS Files app on devices running iOS 12.0 or earlier.

To disable Files app functionality:

  • From the Admin Console, click Enterprise Settings.
  • Click the Mobile tab.
  • In the User permissions for Box Mobile Application section, click the Disable iOS files functionality on devices running iOS 12.0 or older (iOS EMM only) slider button. When you click this slider button, Box automatically disables the Files app functionality for unprotected versions of iOS, and automatically re-enables Files functionality when a protected version of iOS is online.

You need to update your devices to version 4.3.6 of Box for EMM on iOS.

The above applies only to people using iOS EMM. It does not apply to anyone else.

Using the Status-and-Transfers Icon

When you’re

  • uploading or downloading a file or folder,
  • moving or copying a file or folder, or
  • marking for offline access a file or folder, the status-and-transfers icon at the top of the screen displays the current progress of the action. The status-and-transfers icon also enables you to cancel the action, retry a failed action, or retry an action that returned an error.

To see the detailed status of the action: tap the status-and-transfers icon.

To Cancel or Retry the action:

  • Tap the status-and-transfers icon. Box displays the status window.
  • Beside the file or folder name, tap the loading icon and select the option you want to perform.

Viewing Annotated Files with Box for iOS

Box annotations accelerates the review and decision-making process by unifying feedback across desktop, Web, and mobile Box apps. Using only your iOS device, you can:

  • Create and view freeform hand-drawn annotations in Box Preview, and share those annotations with others.
  • Securely view annotations across files, documents, images, and video files without having to open the application in which the content was created.
  • Receive immediate notification of new annotations or feedback when someone mentions you in an annotation comment.
  • View comments in your Box Notification Center. Here’s how to work with Box Annotations on your iOS device:

When someone uses the Box Web app to annotate a document, Box records details in the File Activity pane, including the commenter’s name, the time of the comment, and the page number of the annotated section. (The File Activity pane displays on the right side on iPads, and via the button on iPhones.) When they’re done they can share the annotated document with you via a shared link, or directly notify you by using the @ command and your user name within a comment. You receive an email with a link to the document, plus an alert on your home screen.

Tap the alert (or the emailed link), and Box opens the file preview to the annotated area, regardless of where in the document it may be.

You can view all existing comments in the File Activity pane.

Tap Page # in a comment, and Box immediately displays the page with the corresponding annotation.

You can also view an annotated document on your iOS device by navigating directly to the file you want and then opening it in Box Preview.

Note

Update to the latest version of the Box app if you receive an alert indicating some comments are not visible.

For more information, including a list of file types you can annotate in Box, please see details on how to create annotations using the Box Preview app.

Product basics

What is Box Notes?

Box Notes is a document-creation tool built into Box. You can take notes, format content, add images and tables, share ideas, and collaborate in real time without leaving Box.

How do Box Notes differ from Word, Google Docs, or other file types in Box?

Box Notes are native Box documents. They open in the Box Notes editor in a browser or in the Box mobile apps. They are online-only formats and cannot be made available offline through Box Drive or the Box mobile apps.

Do I need to save a Box Note?

No. Box Notes save automatically to Box as you work. You do not need a separate Save action for normal editing.

Do I need to lock a Box Note before editing?

No. Multiple collaborators can edit the same note in real time. Identifier icons follow each collaborator as they edit or select text.

Is there a public API for Box Notes?

Not at this time.

Creating and editing notes

How do I create a new Box Note?

You can create a blank note in several ways:

  • From the Notes sidebar, click the plus icon next to Notes. Box stores the note in your default My Box Notes folder.
  • From a folder in the Box web app, click New, then Box Note. Box stores the note in the current folder.
  • From an open Box Note, click New.
  • Open https://app.box.com/notes/create_note as a browser bookmark or shortcut. Click the header to set a title. Forward slashes and backslashes are not allowed in titles.
Can I change where newly created notes are stored by default?

Yes. Open any existing Box Note, open the gear menu in the left navigation, and choose Change Default Save Location. Select an existing folder or create a new one.

What content can I add to a Box Note?

In addition to formatted text, you can insert content such as tables, call-out boxes, code blocks, hyperlinks, images, and other blocks from the inline menu. Click the + symbol on the left of the text editor to open that menu.

How do I insert and format tables?

Insert a table from the Notes editor, or copy a table from another source and paste it into the note. Use the cell menu or the table grid controls to add or remove rows and columns, set headers, merge cells, sort columns, change background color, and distribute column widths evenly.

How do I print a Box Note?

Open the More Options menu (ellipsis in the upper-right corner) and select Print. Do not use the browser or operating-system File > Print path. Box documents that printing from the OS File menu does not work correctly because browsers often cannot locate the note content on the page.

Collaboration, sharing, and comments

Who can view or edit my Box Note?

Folder collaborators and folder permissions apply to notes stored in that folder. Anyone who can view the folder can view the note. Anyone with Editor access to the folder can edit it.

You can also invite people to edit a single Box Note without inviting them to the containing folder. Those people receive Editor access to the note only. The note appears in their Files view and can be renamed, but not moved or deleted by that invite method.

Folder-level collaborators still retain their folder permissions even if you also invite people to the individual note.

How do I share a Box Note?

Click Share in the upper-right corner. Common options include:

  • Get Link with Can View for read-only access
  • Get Link with Can Edit for edit access
  • Invite people to edit to add collaborators to the note itself
  • Manage people to review and change collaborators, including people who inherit access from the parent folder A Can Edit shared link also allows recipients to view the note’s version history.
Can anonymous users edit a Box Note through an edit shared link?

No. Users must sign in to Box to edit. Anonymous users cannot edit Box Notes even when the shared link is set to Can Edit.

Can administrators or users disable edit shared links?

Yes.

  • Users can disable Edit Shared Links in Account Settings under Shared Links by choosing Preview the shared item only.
  • Administrators can set default shared-link access or disable Edit Shared Links in Enterprise Settings under Content and Sharing. When Edit Shared Links are disabled, the Can View / Can Edit control is not available.
Why does a password-protected shared link fail to open a Box Note?

Shared links that require a password, or notes in folders that require a password on shared links, are not supported for Box Notes. In that case, the note does not load.

Can Box Notes be used in folders with Hide Collaborators enabled?

No. Box Notes cannot be used in folders that have the Hide Collaborators security property set.

How do comments and annotations work in Box Notes?

Editors and co-owners can highlight text and leave annotations, or open the Comments sidebar to comment on the note. Collaborators can reply, @mention people, and resolve annotations.

Box can send notifications for comments and annotations when the recipient has comment notifications enabled for owned or joined items. Viewers opening a note through a shared link can leave comments on the full document and reply in threads, but cannot leave comments on specific parts of the document.

How can I see what changed since I last opened a note?

When you reopen a note that others have modified, additions made since your last view are highlighted in purple. Use the highlighter control in the upper-right corner to hide or show those highlights.

You can also open Recent Activity from a collaborator badge to see who recently viewed or edited the note, and watch collaboration cursors to see where active editors are working.

How many people can edit a Box Note at once?

Box documents a maximum of 30 people editing a note at the same time. After that limit, additional users see a snapshot or read-only view.

Organization, move, copy, and favorites

How do I move or copy a Box Note?

Open the More Options menu and select Move or copy this note. Choose a destination folder, optionally create a new folder, then choose Move or Copy.

What happens to version history when I move or copy a note?

Moving a note retains its version history. Copying a note does not retain version history.

How do I open the parent folder of a note?

In the left-hand Notes list, click the parent folder name on the note’s row, or use the More Options menu for that note.

How do Favorites work with Box Notes?

Open the Notes sidebar and use the star view to see favorited notes. Mark a note as a favorite from the More Options menu, or click the star next to the note in Recent Notes.

What appears in Recent Notes?

Creating or opening a note adds it to your recents list. Box displays the 1000 most recent notes.

Templates

Can I create a Box Note from a template?

Yes, on paid plans. Templates are not available to free Box accounts.

Create a note from a template from the Notes sidebar (Note from Template) or from the Files page (Box Note from Template). You can use default templates, custom templates you can access as a collaborator, or a template opened from a shared link.

How do I create a custom template?

Create a Box Note, fill it with the structure and content you want, open More Options, and choose Set this as a Template. That note file becomes the template. If you delete it, the template is no longer available.

How do I share a custom template with others?

Common methods:

  • Add people as collaborators on the folder that contains the template so it appears in their Custom template list.
  • Invite them to edit the template directly.
  • Send a shared link. Shared-link recipients must open the template and click Use this Template. Templates shared only by link do not appear in the Custom tab. Collaborators with Viewer Uploader, Editor, Co-owner, or Owner access can edit or disable a template.
How do I disable a template?

Open the template, open More Options, and choose Disable this Template. The template becomes a regular Box Note again. Deleting the template also removes it, but you would need to recreate it later.

Version history and activity reporting

How does Box Notes version history work?

While you work, Box Notes automatically create versions. The version history interface describes saves roughly every 5 minutes, or at the first update after at least 5 minutes of inactivity.

Open More Options, then Version History. The panel lists versions with date, time, and editor. You can preview a past version and choose Restore. Restoring does not discard history. The restored version becomes the current version and is added to the existing history.

Is Notes version history the same as the normal Box file version history?

No. They are separate. The regular Box web app version history is disabled or hidden for Box Notes. Use the Notes version history panel instead.

Can I see exactly who changed which text in a version?

Not at this time. Version history shows the editor associated with a version, but does not identify the exact text each person changed within that version.

Is version history available on mobile?

Not at this time.

How do Box Notes appear in Admin Console reports?

Box Notes are included in Admin Console reports:

  • Creating a note can be recorded as Created or Uploaded.
  • Viewing a note may be recorded as File Opened and may sometimes include a Download.
  • Edits and annotations are recorded as Uploaded. For concurrent editing, the person who made the most recent edit in the reporting interval is listed as the uploader.
  • Deletes are recorded as Trash. Box can provide a more complete Notes activity log on request through a Customer Success Manager or box-notes-log-request@box.com.

Desktop sync and offline access

How do Box Notes work with Box Drive?

In Box Drive, Box Notes remain online-only. They cannot be marked available offline.

Can I use Box Notes without an internet connection?

No. Box Notes require network access in the web app, Box Drive, and Box mobile apps.

Mobile

Can I create and edit Box Notes on iOS and Android?

Yes. Both Box for iOS and Box for Android can create, edit, comment on, and share Box Notes. Changes save automatically. Editor or Co-owner access is required to edit. Other collaborators have view access.

Are tables fully editable on mobile?

No. Existing table content can be edited on iOS, but you cannot create tables or change table structure on mobile. On Android, tables are read-only.

Which newer Notes features are limited on mobile?

The mobile apps still use the current Notes editor for existing content, but several creation and formatting features are restricted. Mobile limitations include:

  • No contextual menus
  • No Tables of Contents
  • Call-out boxes can be viewed, edited, and deleted, but not created or recolored
  • No creating dividers, headers, new font styles, block quotes, Markdown, typography controls, or code blocks
  • Images cannot be resized
Can I use Box AI inside Notes on mobile?

Yes, when Box AI is available for the account. Open a note and tap the Box AI icon to ask questions, extract insights, or generate summaries.

Box AI for Notes

Is Box AI available in Box Notes?

Yes, for Business and above accounts when Box AI for Notes is enabled for the organization. You can generate drafts, refine selected text, ask questions about content, add sources, and insert responses into the note.

How do I start Box AI in a note?

Open a note, click the plus icon, and select Box AI, or use the keyboard shortcut Command/Ctrl + Shift + I. You can also use the Box AI sidebar for suggested prompts such as summarizing the document or identifying key takeaways.

What should I check if Box AI is missing from Notes?

Confirm with an administrator that the organization is provisioned for Box AI and that Box AI for Notes is enabled.

Limits, admin controls, and known issues

What content size limits does Box recommend for Notes?

Box recommends staying within approximately:

  • 200 pages of text, or about 500,000 characters
  • 100 items in a list
  • Images up to 20 MB Exceeding these limits can cause lag, unexpected behavior, or browser tab crashes.
Why is the New Box Note button disabled for some users?

If an administrator enables Restrict content creation, the New Box Note control can be disabled because Notes create content in a first-level folder context for some creation paths. Confirm the Content and Sharing enterprise setting with the administrator.

Which browsers support Box Notes?

Box Notes are supported on current desktop browsers covered by Box’s browser policy, plus iOS Safari and Chrome and Android Chrome for viewing existing notes in mobile browsers.

What firewall hosts should be allowlisted for Box Notes?

Allowlist the hosts listed in Box’s firewall configuration article for Box applications. Incomplete allowlisting can prevent Notes from loading or saving.

What common editor issues should I know about?

Documented known issues include:

  • Images wider than a table cell can overflow the cell border.
  • Wide tables may hide controls until the user attempts sideways scrolling.
  • Structural formatting can be lost when pasting from Notes to Excel desktop, while Excel-to-Notes paste preserves more formatting.
  • Pre-Notes 2.0 Title and Sub-title styles are not included in updated tables of contents unless converted to heading styles.
  • Copying from third-party products can change formatting.
  • Annotations and collaboration cursors are not yet implemented for code blocks.
  • Copying images from third-party sites into a Box Note is not supported.

Troubleshooting

Why will a Box Note not load?

Check these common causes first:

  • The shared link or parent folder requires a password.
  • The folder has Hide Collaborators enabled.
  • The browser or network blocks required Box hosts.
  • The user lacks permission to the note or folder.
  • The note is being opened offline or from a Drive or Sync offline path.
Why can a collaborator view but not edit a note?

Confirm the person’s access level. Editor or Co-owner access is required to edit. Viewer access is view-only. Anonymous shared-link users also cannot edit. Enterprise settings may also disable Can Edit shared links.

Why is Notes performance poor or the browser tab crashing?

Check note size against Box’s recommended limits for text volume, list length, and image size. Large notes can lag or crash the browser tab. Split content, reduce image size, or remove unnecessary embedded content.

Why did a title fail to save?

Remove forward slashes and backslashes from the title. Box does not save titles that contain those characters.

Box Notes in Box for iOS

Box Notes is available in the Box for iOS mobile application. Box Notes are web-based documents and do not require any additional software. You can use Box Notes to create, edit, and share ideas in real-time with your collaborators.

Creating Box Notes

To create a new note, open the Box for iPhone or Box for iPad application on your device and follow this procedure:

  • Navigate to the folder where you’d like to create the new Box Note.
  • Tap the + icon in the top right corner.
  • Tap Create New Box Note. A new note will load immediately.
  • Tap the title to edit and assign a new title for this note.
  • Start typing in your new Box Note. You can add annotations to your Box Note by higlighting text and tapping the Annotate icon in the bottom menu. Tap highlighted text to view annotations left by collaborators.
  • Tap Done to dismiss the keyboard. Editing Box Notes

Like any other Box document, you can find your notes in the folder where you added the note. You can open and edit your Box Note, and all changes will be saved automatically.

While editing your Box Note, use the toolbar at the bottom to change text formatting (screenshot below). Apply changes to existing text by highlighting it before selecting a formatting option.

To add images to your box note, touch the image icon (screenshot above) in the upper right-hand corner and choose the image you would like to add. You can add images from Box, from your iOS library, or you can take a new photo and immediately add it to your Box Note.

Sharing Box Notes

Tap the Shared Link iconin the toolbar at the bottom of your device to generate a shared link to the Box Note. Only collaborators with access levels of Editor or Co-owner can make changes to Box Notes. All other collaborators will only have view access. You can choose to send the shared link directly to collaborators via Email or Messages, or copy the link to the clipboard and paste it later.

Box Notes Notices and Known Limitations

Support Information

Box Notes is supported on the following browsers and versions:

  • iOS Safari and Chrome
  • Android Chrome
  • You can open and view existing Box Notes on mobile browsers.
  • Box for Android: Box Notes is supported on Android KitKat 4.4 and higher.

Reporting Behavior

Box Notes are included in Admin Console Reports.

  • Creating a new Box Note is recorded as Created or Uploaded.
  • Viewing a Box Note may be recorded with File Opened and may sometimes be accompanied by a Download.
  • Edits (and annotations) made to a Box Note are recorded as Uploaded. For edits (Uploaded), the user recorded for the upload is made every 30 seconds; see the Version Behavior section below for details.
  • Deletes of Box Notes are recorded normally as action Trash.

Version Behavior

Box Notes creates a new version of each note in Box every 30 seconds, and lists the author as the person who made the most recent edit. Thus, if two people are making edits simultaneously in a note, the person who made the last edit will be recorded as uploading that version. Box provides a complete log of activities in Box Notes upon a request to your Customer Success Manager (CSM) or to box-notes-log-request@ box.com

Known Limitations

  • Maximum number of people editing a note at the same time: 30
  • Once the limit is reached, any new users will see a snapshot/read only view of the note
  • Recommended maximum content:
    • 200 pages of text (about 500,000 characters)
    • 100 items in a list
    • Images up to 20 MB
    • If these limits are exceeded, the product may act unexpectedly, including lag while typing or browser tab crashes.
  • Shared links to Box Notes that have the “Require Password” option set or that are in folders that have the “Require Password” option set are not supported at this time. In this case, the Box Note will not load.
  • Box Notes cannot be used in folders that have the Hide Collaborators security property set.
  • If an admin has the “Restrict content creation” enterprise setting turned on, the new Box Note button will be disabled because Box Notes creates new notes inside a folder at the first-level.
  • Table object is not editable in Box for Android.
  • In Full Width Mode, tables will always be full width. To narrow the table, you must narrow the first column.
  • Copying images from third-party sites to a Box Note is note supported.

FAQ

Can you change the location of where newly-created notes are stored?

Yes, you can change the default save location for new Notes. To do this, open any existing Box Note. In the lefthand navigation, at the bottom, click the gear icon. From the menu that displays, click Change Default Save Location.

The Select a Default Save Location window opens. Navigate to the folder you want, click its corresponding circle, and then click Save. Or, to save your Notes in a new folder, click New Folder, type in a folder name, and then click Create.

How do I get to the parent folder of a note?

You can click on the name of the parent folder in the left-hand sidebar notes list, in the row of the note. You can also click on the ‘More options’ menu (looks like 3 dots on the right-hand corner) to also get to the parent folder.

What does a company need to consider to ensure it works within their firewall?

We suggest ensuring these URLs are allowlisted: Configuring a Firewall for Box Applications

What constitutes a ‘recent’ note? What factors / date range make a note display in the new sidebar?

When you create or open a note, it is added to your recents list. We display the 1000 most recent notes.

Comments and Annotations in Box Notes

You can comment on a Box Note, or select to highlight any portion of a note and annotate that portion. Each time someone comments on or annotates a file, Box sends email notifications to anyone who owns or has joined the folder that contains the file. This makes it easier for teams to work together and provide quick feedback.

Annotating a Box Note

  • Select to highlight the text you want to annotate.
  • Click the annotation icon.
  • Enter your feedback.
  • Click Post. The text you’ve annotated is highlighted with a yellow background. Your annotation displays whenever someone else hovers over the highlighted text. Text with multiple annotations is highlighted in a brighter, deeper yellow.

Note

Only collaborators with editor or co-owner access can annotate a Box note.

You can also respond to an existing annotation:

  • Hover over the existing annotation
  • Click Reply. Your text is appended to the existing annotation, and your response prompts Box to send out another email notification.

You can also leave a comment on the entire document. To do this:

  • In the top right, click the Comment icon to open the Comments sidebar.
  • Enter your comment
  • Click Post. You can delete any Box Note comments that you added. To delete a collaborator’s comment on a Box Note you own, use the Box API.

@Mention

You can use @mentions to tag someone in the Box Note.

  • Type the @ symbol, followed by the name or email of the people you want to tag.
  • Depending if the user is internal or external, you can:
    1. Invite
  • b. Share a link
  • Select permission level
    1. Editor
  • b. Viewer
  • Once selected, the user you added will have access to the Box note and be sent an email notification, depending on that user’s permission settings.” Note

To receive notifications when a file has been annotated or commented upon, you must enable your notification settings for comments for either “In Items I Own” or “In Items I’ve Joined”. More information on folder settings.

Creating a Box Note

It’s simple and fast to create a new Box Note. The process differs slightly, depending on where you are within Box when you create the Note.

Note

This article explains how to create a new, blank Box Note. You can also create a new Note from a template.

To create a new Box Note in the default Notes folder

  • In the lefthand navigation, next to the Notes listing, click the plus icon. Box automatically stores this note in your default My Box Notes folder.

To create a Note directly into the folder of your choice:

  • Navigate to the folder you want.
  • From the top navigation, click New, and from the list that displays, click Box Note. Box automatically stores your Note in your current folder.

There are two other easy ways to create a new blank Box Note:

  • Directly from an existing Box Note. To do this, open any Box Note, navigate to the top navigation and click New.
  • Via app.box.com. Save this URl as a shortcut or bookmark in your browser. Then click on it to open a new, blank Box Note. In all of the above cases, you can title the note by clicking the header bar (Default title: Add a Title) and type in your own title. When you begin typing, Box also automatically saves your changes.

Note: You can’t use forward slashes and backslashes in the title of your Box Note. Box will not save titles containing these characters.

More on creating Box Notes from templates.

Deleting Box Notes

Users can delete Box Notes from within the Box Notes web interface. To delete a Box Note, open the More Options menu (the ellipses in the upper right) and select “Delete This Note”

Formatting Text in Box Notes

To format text, use the toolbar towards the top of the screen. Formatting text in Box Notes works much the same way as formatting text in a word processor:

  • To format existing text, select a passage and then click the formatting tool you want.

  • To format new text, click the formatting tool you want and then begin typing. Tool options include:

  • Font Title: Choose from body text and heading levels 1 through 3.

  • Font Style: Apply bold, italic, underline, or strikethrough styles.

    • Bold:
      • Click B to apply the bold style
      • CTRL+B keyboard shortcut on PC
      • CMD+B keyboard shortcut on Macs
    • Italics:
      • Click I to apply the italic style
      • CTRL+I keyboard shortcut on PC
      • CMD+I keyboard shortcut on Macs
    • Underline:
      • Click U to apply the underline style
      • CTRL+U keyboard shortcut on PCs
      • CMD+U keyboard shortcut on Macs
    • Strikethrough:
      • Click to apply the strikethrough style
      • CTRL+SHIFT+9 keyboard shortcut on PCs
      • CMD+SHIFT+9 keyboard shortcut on Macs
    • Inline Code:
      • Click </> to apply the code style
      • Use back ticks to apply the code style
      • CTRL+SHIFT+C keyboard shortcut on PCs
      • CMD+SHIFT+C keyboard shortcut on Macs

  • Font Size: Select the size from the dropdown list.

  • Font Color: Select the required color block from the dropdown list.

    • Highlight: Choose a color to highlight text.

  • Text Alignment: Click the arrow to see options to align your text to the left, center, or right of the note.

  • Bulleted Lists, Numbered Lists, or Check Lists: To add bullets to a list click the bullets icon. To add numbers to a list click the number icon. To add a checklist to the note, click the checklist icon. To indent the list further, use the Tab key.

  • Insert Image: See: Inserting Images in Box Notes

  • Insert Table: See: Using Tables in Box Notes

Word and Character Count

While working through a note, you can see the word and character count of the whole document or selecting a portion of text:

  • Open from the ellipsis (…) menu or
  • Mac: Command + Shift + 0
  • Windows: CTRL + Shift + 0 tech_writers_swarm_kb

Inserting and Formatting Tables in Box Notes

Inserting tables

To insert a table into your Box Note:

  • Select the table icon from the top tool bar.

  • Click + from the left context menu and select Table. Box then displays the table in your Box Note. You can now enter text into the table, and format the table to meet your needs

  • If you add rows below a row that has specific justification and then add or paste content in those new rows, the content follows the justification of the row above.

Inserting tables from outside Box Notes

If you have a table from another source, you can copy that table and paste it into the Box Note. All structural formatting and content, including color of the cells, from the table remain the similar after you paste it. You can also copy a table from Box Notes and paste it into another source.

Note: Structural formatting is lost when pasting between Box notes and Excel desktop. See Box Notes Limitations for more information.

Formatting tables

Box provides two ways for you to format a table. You can select from a variety of actions in a cell menu, or use the table’s grid display to add or remove columns and rows.

When you click a cell:

  • Box displays the cell menu icon in the cell’s top-right corner.
  • Box displays the table in grid display with a shaded border and dots along the top and left sides of the table.
Using table menus

Accessing the table menu:

Click the ellispsis menu on the following areas to view specific actions:

  • All areas
    • Background Color
    • Clear Cell(s)
  • Row, Column, Table
    • Delete item
  • Mulitple selected items (Drag and hold)
    • Merge items
  • Side of row
    • Set row header
    • Duplicate row
    • Merge cells
    • Insert above
    • Insert below
  • Top of column
    • Sort Column
      • Ascending
      • Descending
    • Set column header
    • Duplicate column
    • Merge cells
    • Insert left
    • Insert right
  • Cell
    • Insert above
    • Insert below
    • Insert left
    • Insert right
    • Delete row
    • Delete column If you highlight the whole table:
  • Background Color
  • Distribute column
  • Clear Cells
  • Delete Table
Using the table’s grid display

Icons in the table’s grid display enable you to

  • Insert a column to the left or right of a selected column
  • Remove columns
  • Insert a row above or below a selected row
  • Remove rows In contrast to the cell menu, which enables you to insert columns to the right and insert rows below, the table’s grid display enables you to insert columns to both left and right, and insert rows both above and below.

To insert a column via the table’s grid display:

  • Click a cell where you want to insert the column. At the top of the table, Box displays a dot above each of the column’s borders.

  • To add a column to the left, hover on the dot above the column’s left border. To add a column to the right, hover on the dot above the column’s right border. Box displays a + icon.

  • Click +. To remove a column via the table’s grid display:

  • Click the top cell of the column you want to remove. To select multiple columns, click then drag and release. Box displays a shaded border along the top of the table.

  • Click the shaded border above the column. Above the column, Box displays an x icon.

  • Click x. To insert a row via the table’s grid display:

  • Click a cell in a row where you want to insert a new row. On the table’s left side, Box displays a dot beside each of the row’s borders.

  • To add a row above, hover on the dot beside the row’s top border. To add a row below, hover on the dot beside the row’s bottom border. Box displays a + icon.

  • Click +. To remove a row via the table’s grid display:

  • Click a cell in the row you want to remove. To select multiple rows, click then drag and release. Box displays a shaded border along the left side of the table.

  • Click the shaded border beside the row. Beside the row, Box displays an x icon.

  • Click x. To move a row or column

  • Hover over the top of the row or column to select it.

  • Drag and drop the row or column above, below, to the right or left of a another row or column.

Adjusting column width

Box enables you to select a column’s border, and then drag the border to the desired width.

Box also Box enables you to equalize the widths of all columns in a table.

To adjust the width of a column:

  • Hover on a column’s border. Box highlights the border.

  • Click and hold on the highlighted border.

  • Move your mouse left or right, then release. To equalize all column widths:

  • Click in a cell.

  • In the top-right corner of the selected cell, click the menu icon. Box displays a drop-down menu of formatting actions you can select.

  • In the drop-down menu, click Distribute columns evenly. Tip

To cancel an action:

  • On Windows, press and hold your keyboard’s Ctrl key and press the z key.
  • On Mac, press and hold your keyboard’s Command key and press the z key. These key combinations cancel only the immediately preceding action.

tech_writers_swarm_kb

Inserting Block Quotes

You can add block quotes to your Box Notes. When you add a block quote, Box displays a shaded vertical bar to the left of the text that you type or paste. You can also add images to block quotes.

Web Application

On the web application, you can insert a block quote in one of two ways: using the contextual menu or a key combination.

To insert a block quote using the contextual menu:

  • Click where you want to insert the block quote. Box displays + to the left of your cursor.

  • Click + and select Block Quote.

  • Type or paste the quoted text. To insert a block quote using keyboard keys:

  • Click where you want to insert the block quote.

  • On your keyboard, simultaneously press the > and space keys.

  • Type or paste the quoted text. To exit a block quote, press Enter on a blank line, or click outside the block quote.

Mobile Application

On your mobile device, you can insert a block quote by tapping the “>” and space keys at the same time.

To insert a block quote using the keypad:

  • Tap where you want to insert the block quote.
  • On your keypad, simultaneously tap the > and space keys.
  • Type or paste the quoted text. To exit a block quote, tap Enter on a blank line, or tap outside the block quote.

Inserting Call Outs

A Call Out allows you to highlight important information or make your announcements stand out. Use Call Outs to provide tips, warning messages, or any other type of information you perceive as particularly helpful for the user.

  • Click the + icon and select Call Out from the context menu.
  • The call out appears in a new line.
  • Type in the content. The call out is saved automatically.

Customizing call outs

You can customize your call outs to suit your needs and match the content you are working on.

  • The speech bubble emoji that appears on the left is the default emoji. Click it to choose a suitable one.
  • To change the background color, click the ellipsis (…) button and select the color.

Deleting call outs

To delete a call out, click the ellipsis (…) button and select Remove.

Inserting Emojis and Symbols

Box enables you to insert various emojis and symbols into your Box Notes by typing commonly used character combinations.

This feature is available on all supported platforms.

Using Emojis and Symbols

To insert an emoji or symbol, type in the selected character combination and press space key. Box automatically changes the text to an emoji or symbol.

Deleting Emojis and Symbols

To remove an emoji or symbol, do one of the following:

  • On Mac: Press Cmd and Z at the same time.
  • On Windows: press Ctrl and Z buttons at the same time.
  • Press the backspace button to revert an emoji or symbol to text. To remove it completely, keep pressing the backspace button until all characters are deleted.

Inserting Images in Box Notes

You can insert images into Box Notes by dragging and dropping them from your desktop, or by inserting a Box shared link for an image stored on Box.

Insert an image in one of two ways:

  • Drag and drop an image from your desktop into a Box Note. This is the fastest and easiest way.
  • Click the upload icon (up arrow) in the toolbar, and choose either Upload image from your computer or Insert image from Box shared link. When you upload images on your iOS devices, Box stores images in a Box folder in the same directory as the Box Note. The folder is named “Box Notes Images”, and inside the folder is a specific folder named after the title of your Box Note. Box inserts images into Box Notes using shared links with your account’s default access type. If you are sharing a Box Note with someone outside your company, you may need to adjust the access level of the images’ shared links for the images to appear.

When you use the Insert image from Box shared link option, you must use a Box shared link to an image stored on Box. Box Notes does not support external links and non-shared links.

Supported image formats:

Box Notes supports the following image file types:

  • .bmp
  • .gif
  • .ico
  • .jpeg
  • .jpg
  • .png
  • .svg

Resizing images

When you click on an image, Box displays a dot in the middle of each side of the image, and at each corner of the image. Use these dots to resize your images.

When you resize an image, Box maintains the image’s proportions.

To resize an image:

  • Click the image.
  • Do one of the following:
    • On the left or right side of the image, click and hold on the dot, then drag the cursor horizontally.
    • On the top or bottom side of the image, click and hold on the dot, then drag the cursor vertically.
    • On one of the corners of the image, click and hold on the dot, then drag the cursor diagonally.
  • When the image is the size you want, release the mouse button.

Inserting Table of Contents into Box Notes

A heading-based Table of Contents allows you and your collaborators to quickly find the information you are looking for, especially when you come across a longer Box Note.

To insert a Table of Contents:

  • Click the contextual menu on the left and select Table of Contents.

  • The structure of your Table of Contents is based on the headings. When you add or remove a heading, or change a heading type, the Table of Contents updates automatically.

  • Note:

  • The Table of Contents uses Heading 1, 2, and 3 to build the structure. Other types are not supported. To customize a Table of Contents:

  • Click the three dots icon above the Table of Contents to display a pop-up menu.

  • Use the following options to customize the Table of Contents:

    • Hide Contents: Collapses the Table of Contents.
    • Headings: Allows you control the structure by selecting the headings you want to display.
    • Remove: Removes the Table of Contents.

Introducing Box Notes

Box Notes is an easy-to-use document creation tool that functions natively in Box.

With Box Notes, you can quickly take notes, share ideas, and collaborate in real-time with your team – all without leaving Box.

Navigation and organization

In addition to all the helpful features you see, you can insert additional content such as tables, call out boxes, and code blocks from the inline menu. Click the + symbol on the left of the text editor to open the menu select which content block you want to add.

Known Issues: Box Notes

This topic summarizes known issues with Box Notes.

Tables

  • If an image is added to a table cell that is wider than the width of the cell, the image will overflow the border of the table cell.
  • When a table is wider than the browser viewport, some of the table controls may not always be visible. For example, you may not see a horizontal scroll bar until you attempt to scroll sideways.
  • Structural formatting is lost when pasting from Box Notes to Excel desktop, however, formatting is keep when pasting from Excel desktop to Box Notes.

Tables of Contents

  • Because Box Notes 2.0 no longer offers Title or Sub-title paragraph styles, pre-Box Notes 2.0 documents that used those styles will not be included in updated tables of contents. Change any paragraphs styles with Title or Sub-Title to any heading-level style to have those paragraphs appear in tables of contents.

Images

  • If an image is added to a table cell that is wider than the width of the cell, the image will overflow the border of the table cell.

Copy & Paste

  • Because many products format content and images in many different ways, you may see slight formatting changes when you copy from those products and paste into a Box Note.

Lists

  • Adjacent lists of different types do not always adjust list type correctly when merged into a single list.

Code Blocks

  • Annotations & Collaboration Cursors are not yet implemented for Code Blocks.

On-Demand Conversion of Classic Editor to New Editor

  • Alignment that has been applied to lists will not be preserved. (The Classic Editor allowed you to apply left, center, or right alignment to lists. The New Editor disables this text alignment for lists, so when Notes are converted to the New Editor, any alignment that was applied in the Classic Editor is removed.)
  • Table column sizes will only be accurately preserved if they are based off a standard width (not full width) table.
  • Hyperlinks applied to images will not be preserved.

Mobile Compatibility

Box Notes, when access through Mobile, will still be powered by the New Editor, but users won’t have access to all of the new features in their Mobile UI. Rest assured, users can still interact with all of the various new components in Notes they have already created, but their ability to insert objects, such as Call Out Box, will be restricted. This section lists these issues.

  • Users do not have access to contextual menus in the native mobile app.
  • User do not have access to Tables of Contents in the native mobile app.
  • Users will have access to view, edit, and delete Call Out Boxes in native mobile app, but not the ability to create Call Out Boxes, or update the background color.
  • Users do not have access to create dividers in the native mobile app.
  • Users do not have access to create headers, new font styles, or styling in the native mobile app. If these objects are already in Notes they have created, they can interact with them, but not create new ones.
  • Users cannot resize images in the native mobile app.
  • Users do not have access to create Block Quotes in the native mobile app.
  • Users do not have access to use Markdown in the native mobile app.
  • Users do not have access to use Typography in the native mobile app.
  • Users do not have access to create, edit, or delete Code Blocks in native mobile app.

Moving or Copying Box Notes

To move or copy a Box Note:

  • Open the More Options menu (ellipses in the upper right corner) and select Move or copy this note.
  • In the window that appears, select a destination folder by clicking the bubble beside its name. If you do not select a folder, the file will be moved or copied into the folder that you are currently viewing.
  • Alternatively, you can create a new folder (inside the folder you are currently viewing) by clicking New Folder.
  • Click Move or Copy complete the action. tech_writers_swarm_kb

Opening or Searching for Box Notes

From within the Box Notes web interface, you can open any Box Note that you have access to. You can also search for any Box Note you have access to.

Opening Box Notes

To open a Box Note:

  • From your Files page, in the lefthand navigation click Notes to open your default Box Notes folder.
  • Click the folder icon () in the upper left corner of the toolbar.
  • In the window that opens, select the Box Note you would like to open by clicking the bubble beside its name. You can also search for a Box Note using the search bar in the pop-up. Click Choose when you have selected a Box Note. To return to a previously opened Box Note, access it from your Recents.

Searching Box Notes

To search for a note:

  • Click the search icon () in the upper left.
  • Enter your search terms in the search bar that displays.
  • Click a result to open that note.

Sharing Your Box Notes

There are three common ways to share your Box Notes with collaborators:

  • Generate a View-only Shared Link if you would like to give someone quick read-only access to the document.
  • Generate an Edit Shared Link if you would like to give someone the ability to edit the Box Note.
  • If you would like others to be able to edit your Box Note, you can add them as collaborators to an individual Box Note, without inviting them to the Box Note’s containing folder.

To share your Box Note

Click the Share button in the upper-right. Three options will be displayed:

  • Click the first option (Get Link) to see a shared link to your file. You can choose whether the recipient of the link:
    • Can View (Viewer permissions)
    • Can Edit (Editor permissions). Be aware that marking the link Can Edit will allow recipients to view the version history of the note.
  • Use the second option (Invite people to edit) to invite collaborators to edit a single Box Note specifically. Simply enter a name or email address and click Send Invites. Invited collaborators will receive an email invitation to collaborate, just like when invited to collaborate on a folder. They will be added to the file with the access level Editor, and will only have access to the Box Note, not its containing folder. The shared Box Note will appear in the collaborator’s Files page. It can be renamed, but not moved or deleted.
  • Click the third option (Manage people) to view a list of all of the collaborators in a particular Box Note. This list will include any collaborators in the containing folder as well. From here, you can add and remove collaborators, as well as manage their access levels. Note: Box Notes will continue to inherit all folder settings regarding collaboration as well. Inviting collaborators to edit a single Box Note will not prevent collaborators at the folder level from being able to edit the Box Note as well.

Different types of Box users have the following abilities:

  • Users can disable Edit Shared links in the Sharing tab of their Account Settings using the Link Viewers Can setting in the Shared Links. Choose the option “Preview the shared item only” to disable Edit Shared Links.
  • Administrators can choose the default access level for shared links or disable Edit Shared Links option in the Content and Sharing tab of their Enterprise Settings. If your Admin has disabled Edit Shared Links, you will not see the Can View/Can Edit drop down.
  • Anonymous Box users will not be able to edit Box Notes, even using an Edit Shared Link. Users must log into Box to edit.
  • Shared links to Box Notes that have the “Require Password” option set or that are in folders that have the “Require Password” option set are not supported at this time. In this case, the Box Note will not load. Multiple collaborators can make changes to Box Notes, simultaneously, without worrying about version control or overwritten content. Identifier icons follow each collaborator as they make changes or select text to annotate throughout the document. Identifier icons are usually a user’s profile picture, but, in the absence of profile pictures, a user’s initials are represented graphically.

Modifying Shared Links

You can also modify the view or edit options after a shared link has been sent. Simply open the Shared Link options and change the setting to Can Edit. But beware that all users who can access this link will also be able to edit. If you want to adjust permissions for different users of the same link, use Collaborator permission levels at the folder level instead.

Tracking Changes and Recent Activity in a Box Note

Box Notes Differences, Presence and Collaboration Cursors make it easier to see what’s specifically changed in a particular Box Note, and who’s been active there.

Tracking Changes with Differences

We’ve made it easy to keep track of changes made by other collaborators. When you open a Box Note that has been modified, any additions made since the last time you viewed the Box Note will be highlighted in purple.

To hide these highlights, simply click the highlighter icon in the upper right corner.

Tracking Recent Activity with Presence

You can keep track of who has viewed or edited a Box Note by clicking on any collaborator’s badge (their profile picture or initials), displayed in the upper right. This will open the Recent Activity tab, where you will see a list of collaborators, sorted by when they last viewed or edited the Box Note. Note that if a collaborator has been invited to the Box Note, but has never opened it, they will not appear in this list.

Tracking Recent Edits with Collaboration Cursors

You can see where other collaborators are working in the file. When someone’s editing a Box Note you’re viewing, a colored cursor displays the editor’s name and icon on hover next to their current edit. Each time a collaborator moves a cursor, Box updates the location of the cursor.

tech_writers_swarm_kb

Tracking Version History in Box Notes

While you’re working in Box Notes, we automatically save your changes as a new version roughly every 5 minutes or at the first update after at least 5 minutes of inactivity. You can access past versions of a Box Note by clicking the More Options menu (the ellipsis in the top right corner), then clicking Version History.

A version history panel will open to the right of your Box Note with the current version at the top of the list. For each version, you will be able to see the date and time the version was saved and the editor associated with that version.

You can select any past version to view it, and you can click Restore for any of the past versions listed to make that version current. This action will not cause any history to be lost. The restored version will be added on to the existing version history as the current version.

Using Code Blocks in Box Notes

To enhance your collaboration during code development and review, Box’s web app enables you to add code blocks to your Box Notes.

In Box Notes, a code block contains a scrollable text field, a language selection field, and a selection to remove the code block.

After adding a code block, you can either paste or type code into your code block’s text field.

Code blocks in Box Notes support the following software languages:

  • Bash shell

  • C

  • C++

  • C#

  • CSS

  • Dart

  • Go

  • HTML

  • JavaScript

  • Perl

  • PHP

  • PowerShell

  • Python Java

  • R

  • Ruby

  • Rust

  • Scala

  • SQL

  • Swift IMPORTANT:

  • After selecting a language for your code block, you cannot select a different language for that code block.

  • Box Notes does not support the use of code blocks on mobile devices. As with all content in Box Notes, multiple people can simultaneously edit a code block’s contents.

When someone is working in your code block’s contents, Box displays a collaboration icon in the code block’s text field identifying the person’s user name.

Collaborators with Read-only permission can view but not edit a code block’s contents.

Note: Box Notes does not support the insertion of other Box Note elements — for example, tables, images, call-out boxes, headings, or other code blocks — into code blocks. To learn more about using other Box Notes elements, start here.

To insert a code block in a Box Note:

  • Click where you want to insert a code block. Beside the cursor, Box displays +.

  • Click + then select Code Block.

  • Type or paste the code into your code block’s text field. To select a software language for your code block:

  • In the top-left corner of the code block, click the menu icon. Box displays a drop-down menu.

  • In the drop-down menu, click the software language you want to use. After selecting a language, you cannot select a different language for this code block. To search for and select a software language for your code block:

  • In the top-left corner of the code block, click the menu icon. Box displays a drop-down menu.

  • In the Search Languages field, type the name of the software language you want to use. As you type, Box displays available languages.

  • Click the software language you want to use. After selecting a language, you cannot select a different language for this code block. To remove a code block:

  • In the top-right corner of the code block, click the ellipsis, “…”.

  • Select Remove. To increase or reduce a code block’s height:

  • Hover your mouse in the code block, then right-click.

  • To increase height, click Expand. To decrease height, click Collapse. Adding a Mermaid Diagram

To help with visualizing logic procedures and operations, you can create a Mermaid diagram in several ways:

  • From the context menu: Click the “+” menu and select Mermaid directly — the language is pre-selected.
  • From a code block: Add a code block, then choose Mermaid from the language dropdown.
  • Using Box AI: Ask Box AI (inline or from the side panel) to generate diagrams and charts for you. You can also highlight a table and ask inline AI to generate a Mermaid pie chart from it.

Using Favorites with Box Notes

View Favorites

Mark a Box Note as a Favorite

To mark a Box Note as a favorite, open the More Options (…) menu in the Box Note that you’d like to favorite, then select Favorite. Alternatively, you can locate the Box Note in the Recent Notes sidebar and click the star icon beside its name.

Using Templates in Box Notes

Templates enable you to quickly create a Box Note using pre-populated content. You can choose from a set of default templates, or use custom templates that you or your team has created. This is useful when you need to create a Box Note using a standard format or structure such as meeting agendas, project plans, or calendars.

Note

Currently, this feature is not available to free Box accounts.

  • Creating a Note Using Templates
    • Default Templates
    • Custom Templates in which you are a collaborator
    • Custom Templates sent to you via shared link
  • Creating a Custom Template
  • Sharing a Custom Template
  • Editing a Custom Template
  • Disabling Specific Templates

Creating a Note Using Templates

You can create a new Box Note from an existing template either in a default Box Notes folder or in the folder in which you are currently active.

To create a new Box Note from a template in your default Box Notes folder:

  • In the Box Notes side navigation, next to the New button, click the arrow.

  • In the dropdown list that displays, click Note from Template. This creates the new note in your default Box Notes folder. Typically the label of this folder is My Box Notes. To create a new Box Note from a template in the folder in which you are currently active:

  • In the Box Web App, on the Files page, click New.

  • In the dropdown list that displays, click Box Note from Template. This creates the new note in your currently active folder. Default Templates To use one of the default templates provided by Box:

  • Select a template under the Default tab.

  • Click Create. This creates a new note that uses template you selected. To use a custom template that you have created or in which you are a collaborator:

  • Open the Custom tab.

    • Any custom templates accessible to you display in this list.
    • Select a template from the list and click Create. A new note is created using the selected template. Note

If you cannot find a template that you believe you should have access to, verify that you are a collaborator in the template itself or in the folder in which the template is located.

Alternatively, you can open the template that you want to use (just as with any Box Note), then, in the top right, click Use this Template.

A new Box Note is created using the template you have opened.

To use a custom template to which you have received a shared link: Templates sent via shared link do not display in the Custom tab of the Template Picker. You must click the shared link you were sent to open the template (just as with any Box Note). Then, in the top right, click Use this Template. A new Box Note is created using the template you have opened.

Creating a Custom Template

To create a custom template:

  • Create a new Box Note.

  • Fill this new note with the contents of your template.

  • Once you are satisfied with your template, open the More Options (…) menu in the upper right corner and select Set this as a Template. This note is now a template. Notes:

  • After you have set a Box Note as a template, that Box Note file is the template file. If you delete this file, no one can use the template. You may want to move the newly-created template into a specific Templates folder, to keep track of where your templates are stored.

  • If you would like others in your organization to use this template, verify that they are collaborators (with any access level) in the template itself, or in the folder in which the template is stored. You can also send coworkers a shared link to the template. This enables them to use the template. However, templates sent to coworkers via shared link do not display in their Custom Templates list.

Sharing a Custom Template

There are a few different ways that you can share a template with a coworker:

  • Add Collaborators to the Folder Containing the Template
    • The best way to ensure a coworker has access to a template is to add that coworker as a collaborator in the folder containing the template. Collaborators (with any access level) in the folder containing a template can select the template from the Custom tab when creating a Box Note from a template.
  • Collaborators with the Viewer Uploader, Editor, Co-Owner, or Owner access level also can edit and disable the template.
    • This method of sharing a template is useful if you want someone to have access to a template in the Custom tab, without giving them permission to edit the template. By inviting them into the folder, you have the most granular control over what permissions they have in relation to the template.
  • Invite to Edit the Template Directly
    • To display a template in someone’s Custom tab when creating a Box Note from a template – and if you are satisfied with giving that person permission to edit the template – you can add them as an Editor to the template itself (just as with any Box Note). To add someone as an Editor in the Template:
      • In the upper-right corner, click Share.
      • Select Invite people to edit.
      • Enter the people you want to add as Editors. Note that they can edit and disable the template. If you do not want to assign these permissions to them, we recommend you add them as collaborators to the folder containing the template. In that way you have more granular control over their permissions.
    • Once someone has been added as an Editor in a Template, the template displays in their Custom tab when creating a Box Note from a template.
  • Send the Template via Shared Link
    • The simplest way to share a template with someone is to send them a shared link to that template. However, templates sent via shared link do not display in the Custom tab of the Template Picker. To use the template, people must click the shared link to open the template, and then, in the top right, click Use this Template. To send a template via shared link:
      • In the upper-right corner, click Share.
      • Click Get Link.
      • Choose who can access this link. You can choose between People in your company, People in this folder, and People with the link.
      • Choose what permission level to assign to people who follow the shared link. Click Can View if you give people with the link access to use the template but not edit or disable it. Click Can Edit to people with the link permission also to edit and disable the template.
      • When you are ready, copy the link provided and send it to whomever you want. Editing a Custom Template

The creator of a template and collaborators with the Viewer Uploader, Editor, Co-Owner, or Owner access level can edit existing templates. To edit a Template:

  • Open the template you wish to edit.
  • Open the the More Options (…) menu and click Edit this Template. You can now edit the template just as with any Box Note. Your changes are saved automatically.

Disabling Specific Templates

The creator of a template and collaborators with the Viewer Uploader, Editor, Co-Owner, or Owner access level can disable existing templates. To disable a template:

  • Open the template you wish to disable
  • Open the the More Options (…) menu and click Disable this Template. The template is converted back to a regular Box Note.

Alternatively, you can delete the template altogether. However, this means you must recreate the template from scratch should you wish to use it again in the future.

Box Notifications

Login activity email repeatedly sent

If login activity emails are enabled in your account, Box sends “Box login from {application_name}” the first time you sign in from a new device or app. This article explains when that notification is sent and why it can sometimes feel like it arrives often.

What is this email?

Box sends this email when an application or connection is newly added to your login activity list. That often happens the first time you use a browser or app you have not used with Box before, or when you sign in from a private or incognito window (because Box may treat that session as a new device).

The message is a security notification so you can confirm that you recognize the app and the approximate time and location of the sign-in.

Why am I getting this email when I’m on a device I’ve used before?

In general, Box sends this notification when the sign-in looks like it is coming from a new device in your login activity.

Web browser: Activity is often tied to browser cookies. If your browser is set to clear cookies when you close it, Box may treat each new session as a new device. In that case, you might get this email each time you open the browser and sign in to Box again.

Apps and API access: The first token request for an app usually registers as a new application connection in login activity. After that, routine token refresh (when an app quietly renews access with a refresh token) is not meant to trigger this email.

Some integrations are built differently. They may run through a full authorization flow (similar to going through Authorize again and getting a new grant) more often than a single “first-time” connection. For example, a web integration that requests a new token using an authorization code every time you open it from Box can cause this notification whenever you use that integration. If you started that activity, you can safely ignore the email. If you did not add the app and do not recognize the activity, use the link in the email or your Security settings to remove the app and consider changing your password and contacting your administrator.

Notifications not sent or multiple notifications sent

Some Box email notifications may not be delivered, may arrive later than expected, or may be sent more than once.

This is a known issue that Box is actively working to resolve. It is not caused by your account, folder, or notification settings, and there is no Admin Console setting or configuration change that prevents it.

Notification types currently affected

  • File comment/mention
  • User deleted and content transferred
  • Tasks Notification types with improved reliability

Reliability for the following notification types has improved significantly, and missed, delayed, or duplicate notifications are now much less frequent:

  • Download, upload, move, and copy collaboration notifications
  • Item deleted by collaborator Box is continuing to improve reliability for these notification types.

Preview notifications

Preview notifications are currently turned off and are not being sent. Box will update this article if preview notifications become available again.

What you can do

If you are seeing missed, delayed, or duplicate notifications, contact Box Support and include:

  • The notification type affected
  • The file or folder involved
  • The expected recipients
  • The approximate date and time of the action that should have triggered the notification These details allow Box to investigate specific occurrences.

Notifications sent to alternate email address

When the Automatically accept incoming collaboration invitations setting is enabled in the Admin Console, the invitation mails to collaborate on folders may be sent to alternate notification email address, even though the Allow all users to receive Box notifications at an alternate notification email address setting has been deactivated.

This behavior depends on the notification type and processing. If you suspect that an invitation to collaborate on folder was sent to you, but you don’t have any information about it on your primary email address, please check your alternate email address.

For more information about notifications settings, see Manage Notifications for Enterprise Users.

Troubleshooting Issues with Email Notifications

If you have configured your email notifications settings to your personal preferences but are still not receiving the notifications as expected, follow the steps below. For example, if you are not notified when your colleague uploads a new file to your shared folder but have the setting turned on.

Troubleshooting Steps

  • Check your Spam/Junk email folder. Sometimes, certain email clients do not recognize email from box.com. If you find Box messages in your Spam or Junk folder, add noreply@box.com to your email contacts, or Safe senders list. This will allow most mail clients to recognize Box emails and deliver them to your Inbox.
  • Firewall, Content Filter, or Email Security Policy: Check if your firewall or virus scan is blocking the email notifications. Contact your Internet Service Provider (ISP) or Corporate IT department and ask that emails from the following domains be added to the email allow list (safe sender) to ensure that Box messages are not blocked.
    • box.com
    • notify.box.com
    • reply.box.com
    • track.box.com
  • Incorrectly typed email address: Is the sender using your correct email address? Just one mistyped letter will cause an email to go to the wrong address or make it undeliverable. Ask them to double-check that they entered your address correctly.
  • Email on suppression list: If Box notifications ever bounce, emails are automatically added to our suppression list. If the email address(es) is correct and able to receive emails, it can be removed from our suppression list. To do so:
    • Log in to the Admin Console and navigate to the Notifications settings.
    • Remove the affected email address(es) using the Suppression List feature.
    • One avoidable reason for getting on the Box suppression list is from creating a new Box account before your actual mailbox or email account is set up.
  • Email scanning issues: If you are experiencing scanning issues, check the HTML code of the templates for any changes and adjust your scripts.
  • Unconfirmed email address: Box does not send most email notifications (with a few exceptions such as password reset and email confirmation messages) to an address that has not been confirmed. If you have not confirmed your email address for your Box account, complete the confirmation step first. After your email address is confirmed, try the action again (for example, folder activity notifications or “Email all” collaborator messages). Note: Box “batches” email notifications before sending them out. This means an email may not be sent immediately after an action occurs. When multiple actions are batched/grouped into a single notification, the subject of the email will have the title of the top-level folder. This does not apply to Password Reset emails or Email Confirmation links.
