Security Key MFA Troubleshooting

To troubleshoot a security key:

  • Make sure it’s securely connected.
  • Test a different USB port.
  • Skip USB hubs or adapters and plug it straight into the computer.
  • Try it on another device.
  • Address potential browser problems by switching to Chrome, Firefox, or Safari, keeping the browser up to date, and verifying the key responds during login.
  • Examine system settings. Reset Windows Hello if needed, and review Event Viewer for error logs.
  • Swap in another security key or apply any pending updates (such as Duo notifications). Simple fixes like restarting your computer or updating your browser often resolve the problem quickly.

Note: If you cannot use the security key on your Box mobile app, please contact Box Support.

Shared Links Frequently Asked Questions

General

What happens if I disable a shared link?

For security purposes, disabled shared links are deleted and cannot be added back to a file or folder. If the shared link is later re-enabled, a new unique URL is generated to ensure the content is only available to those with access to the new link. The behavior is the same on custom links – once it is disabled that link is deleted and is no longer assigned to that file or folder.

Note

Disabling a shared link frees the link back up to be used by someone else on that account, so there could potentially be another file/folder with the same custom link in the future.

How can I tell for sure that I’m sharing content only with the people I want?

Box displays a range of visual indicators and alerts to ensure you do not accidentally share content with anyone you do not specify. More on Box’s security indicators.

I got this error message: “This shared file or folder link has been removed or is unavailable to you.” What do I do?

This error typically is caused by one of 3 things:

  • Incorrect sharing permissions on the shared file. In other words, whoever created the link did not set the correct access level on the link. If you are not already a collaborator in the folder (or file) the link points to, the link would need to be set to “people in the company” (if that person is also at your company) or “people with the link” (if that person is not part of your company).

  • The person who created the shared link has since removed it.

  • You are attempting to access the shared file with a personal Box account instead of the account with which the file was shared. Here’s what you can do:

  • Verify you are logging into Box with the account to which the file was shared. Typically this will be your company Box account.

  • If that doesn’t resolve the issue, contact the individual who owns the file. Ask them to either to review and revise the file share permisions or to send you the correct link to the file.

  • If that doesn’t resolve the issue, contact your organization’s IT admin for help locating the file and fixing the permissions.

  • If the permissions and location of the file are verified and correct, and you still cannot access it, please contact Box Support for assistance at support.box.com.

What happens if a file is deleted while it has an active shared link, but is later restored?

If you delete an item with a shared link and then restore it from trash, the original link is maintained.

Note

Customized shared links are not maintained.

What happens if someone who shouldn’t have access to a file or folder tries to use the shared link?

If you set a shared link to ‘Company’ or ‘Collaborators Only’ and a user that is not one of these access types accesses the link, they will receive an error message saying the item is unavailable.

Shared link expiration dates

Are any approvals required after I set an expiration period?

No. When you save your configuration Box applies the settings system-wide. No further approval or review is required to disable the links.

How can I tell if and when a link is set to expire? Can I change that date?

If a file has a link that is set to expire, it displays with a small red clock icon (). To find the expiration date, do one of the following:

  • In your files list, at the end of the row displaying your file, click Share. Box opens a window that contains the file sharing details. Hover your mouse pointer over the red clock icon. A message displays that indicates the link expiration date
  • In your files list, click to highlight the row displaying your file. File details display in the righthand pane. Under View Details, Box displays the file link’s expiration date. You can change the expiration date, if your Box Admin has enabled that capability. Use the same procedure to change an expiration date as you did to set it originally.

When you preview a file you can also see if it has a link that is set to expire. In the Details pane, Box displays a yellow banner that indicates the existing shared link is set to expire.

If someone shares a link with me, am I notified when it’s about to expire?

You get notified only if you own the files or folders to which the link goes. You get notified by email.

Some users do not appear when you search for a folder’s collaborators

Issue

When searching for collaborators in the Box folder via More Options > More Actions > Manage Collaborators, sometimes you cannot find the expected users as collaborators.

Root Cause

The folder’s collaborator search function can display a maximum of 25 collaborators.

Resolution

Search using the email addresses or other attributes of target users to keep the search results under 25 collaborators.

Sort Files and Folders

You can sort your files and folders by Name, Date Modified, and Size. Simply click the appropriate header to sort.

Click the squares icon to show the files in a grid image format. Click the lines icon to show the files in a list format.

When you define a sorting order in your Files window, Box applies that sorting order as the default sorting order in all your Box windows.

For numbered files that go into double digits (or higher), “0” must be used to fill digit spaces for the numbers to display correctly. For example, if you have a list of items that goes to 15, use “01” instead of “1” for the order to display correctly.

Storage Usage Or File Count In My Account Is Incorrect

On occasion, you may find data inaccuracies on your account, which could be in the form of:

  • Storage allotment in the Admin Console (displayed on graphs or your managed users may tell you that they keep deleting content, but aren’t reclaiming the storage space) Note: This is only applicable if you are the Admin or Co-Admin of your company’s enterprise.
  • Your account says you are “out of free space” even though you know you are not (you may have tried deleting things, but the storage space in not reclaimed; you have added up the file sizes yourself)
  • Folder storage size
  • Folder file counts (ex. the folder has 5 items, but it says it only has 4 in it)
  • “Updated by” person (ex: user John last updated a file, yet it still says that the person who edited it before him was the last to update it)
  • “Updated by” timestamp (ex: you know you edited the file on Tuesday, yet it reports Monday) Note

If you ever come across these data inaccuracies in your account, please know that the problem is entirely with the display of these totals. This has no effect on your underlying data. All of your files remain in place and have not decreased in size or been edited by unauthorized people.

Keep in mind the following information about storage calculations:

  • Trash is excluded from your overall storage calculation.
  • If you are collaborating with another user in a folder they own, the storage is calculated only as part of the owner’s account and will not count toward your storage calculation.

Why does this happen?

A folder will often have several sub-folders, with additional sub-folders below them (and so on). Within each sub-folder, there can be files that are continuously being added, edited, and deleted by multiple people at any given moment. The countless activities, combined with the massive scale at which Box supports, makes it incredibly difficult to accurately display aggregated data points throughout our product at all times. If a folder’s storage space calculation is inaccurate due to these issues, the inaccuracies also impact the overall storage calculations for both the user and Enterprise.

How can Box help?

Most of the time, aggregates will be updated within an hour (for example the user aggregates) or less. For larger changes or more complex folder structures, aggregates may take up to 24 hours to be correct. In rare cases, the file count and size might take few days to a week to be updated.

webapp_swarm_kb

There was a problem while trying to transfer item ownership to {email}.

When attempting to transfer ownership of a folder to another user, you may receive the error “There was a problem while trying to transfer item ownership to {email}.”

Common Causes

The error typically occurs as the transfer was blocked by enterprise settings configured by the Box Admin. Please reach out to the Box Admin to see if any of the following settings are enabled.

  • Restrict content creation
    • Same-enterprise transfers
      • If this setting is enabled, admins (the main admin and co-admins with Manage Users or Manage Groups privilege) can transfer ownership of folders to managed users.
      • Managed users generally cannot transfer ownership to others.
    • Cross-enterprise transfers
      • Source Enterprise Restriction: If the source enterprise has Restrict Content Creation enabled, managed users cannot transfer folders to any internal or external users.
      • Destination Enterprise Restriction: If the destination enterprise has Restrict Content Creation enabled, managed users cannot receive folders at their root level.
      • However, admins (the main admin and co-admins with Manage Users or Manage Groups privilege) in destination enterprise can receive root-level transfers and subsequently assign them to the target user.
  • Retention Policy / Legal Hold
    • You cannot transfer the ownership of a file or folder with a retention policy to an external user.
    • For a relatively large folder (50 files or more), you cannot transfer the ownership to an external user regardless of whether any of the policies actually apply to the contents under that folder.

Resolution Steps

The Box admin can try the followings for each of the scenarios:

  • Restrict content creation
    • Same-enterprise transfers
      • Box Admin or Co-admin with access to Content Manager can perform the ownership transfer through Content Manager on behalf of the managed user.
    • Cross-enterprise transfers
      • Source Restricted: Box Admin or Co-admin with access to Content Manager can perform the ownership transfer through Content Manager on behalf of the managed user.
      • Destination Restricted: The original owner can perform transfer to the admin (the main admin and co-admins with Manage Users or Manage Groups privilege) in destination enterprise, who can then transfer it to the destination user.
  • Retention Policy / Legal Hold
    • Files/folders under retention cannot be moved to an external user. In case transfer of a folder to an external user is blocked even though it doesn’t contain files/folders that are under retention, you can try perform the transfer in a smaller chunk (less than 50 files at a time).
    • If this does not work, please open up a case with our support team and provide the following information:
      • Current owner
      • New owner
      • Folder ID
      • Network capture while attempting transfer

Tracking File Activity in Different Applications

With the wide range of applications you can use to work with a file – sharing the file via apps such as Slack, processing it via apps such as DocuSign, storing it in apps such Salesforce, and so on – it is difficult to track each and every action you have taken. Box addresses this via the Integration Activity stream.

When you preview a file in Box, Integration Activity lists at a glance all of someone’s actions involving a Box file across third-party apps designated for that person – for example, when they shared a file via a Slack message or attached a file to a Salesforce or NetSuite record. This eliminates the need to search through multiple applications to account for every time they may have acted on a file. Instead, the Integration Activity stream makes it easy for people to quickly discover when and to whom they sent a file via Slack, or pushed a document through a DocuSign workflow, or attached a contract to a Salesforce or NetSuite record, and so on.

It also includes when others in your organization have taken these types of actions. For example, it can display all the times a co-worker shared a file via a public Slack channel, or even a private Slack channel of which you’re a member. (This does not apply to a co-worker who has opted out of displaying their integration activity.)

Box begins recording file activity immediately after a Box admin turns on Integration Activity and configures the integration for your organization. It continues recording and accruing file activity from that point forward. There is no time limit – that is, it saves and displays all file events it’s permitted to, regardless of their age. In this way, Integration Activity gives you a single source of truth with regard to when and how you’ve used a document across certain apps in your organization’s ecosystem, as well as to how others in your organization have used the document (depending on your permissions to view).

What apps are included?

Current apps include:

  • Slack
  • Send to DocuSign
  • Box for Salesforce
  • Box for NetSuite However, APIs enable any third-party developer to feature their Box integration in the Integration Activity stream, and more third-party app integrations are coming.

Using the Integration Activity Stream

Preview a Box file. In a separate pane on the right, Box displays a unified view of all the actions taken on that file across third-party apps.

If you don’t see this view, the activity pane is collapsed into a narrow bar on the right. Click the ellipsis (…) at the top of the bar to expand the pane and view all activity.

To view details of any specific action, click in the row of the activity you want. In the below example, previewing a sales distribution contract reveals four discrete actions that have been taken on that file, including sharing it via Slack. Click the Slack listing, and Slack opens and displays the message in which you shared the sales contract.

What file actions are listed

For the most part, Integration Activity works the same way regardless of the application whose activity it displays. However, it may be helpful to understand what specific file events per application you can access. Below are details for each current integration.

Integration Activity for Slack

When you have shared a Box file via Slack – either by previewing the file in Box and then clicking the Slack Recommended Web Integration, or by pasting the link directly in the Slack message window – Integration Activity links directly to the message in Slack where the file was shared. Further, Box records Slack activity regardless of whether you share a file via a Slack direct message or via a Slack private channel.

Here it is in the Slack interface:

And here it is in Box Preview:

Important

You ONLY see Slack activity in Box IF you have access to view that activity when you’re in Slack. Box maps its permissions to those in Slack. That means to access a Box file you share in Slack, you must have permission BOTH to the channel in Slack AND to the file in Box. In the context of app activity, that means Box records a file event in your Integration Activity stream only if you also have the appropriate permission in both Box (to the file) and Slack (to the channel).

Integration Activity for Send to DocuSign

Integration Activity links to details about DocuSign events when:

  • You send a Box file for signature via the DocuSign Recommended Web Integration

  • You sign a Box file in DocuSign that was sent for signature using the DocuSign integration Details include:

    • The original file that was sent for signature through DocuSign integration
    • The envelope status page in DocuSign
    • The signed file that was uploaded back to Box through the DocuSign integration Here it is before the signature, in DocuSign:

Here it is before the signature, in Box Preview:

Integration Activity for Box for Salesforce

When you use the Box for Salesforce integration to attach a Box file to a Salesforce record (such as account, opportunity, lead, and so on) via the Salesforce embed widget, Integration Activity links directly to the Salesforce record to which the file was attached.

Important

Before you can add Salesforce file activity to the Box Integration Activity stream, you must configure it.

Here it is in the Salesforce interface:

And here it is in Box Preview:

Integration Activity for Box for NetSuite

When you use the Box for NetSuite integration to attach a Box file to a NetSuite record (such as a purchase order) via the NetSuite embed widget, Integration Activity links directly to the NetSuite record to which the file was attached.

Important

To install Integration Activity for NetSuite, please contact your Box Account Team for details.

Here it is in the NetSuite interface:

And here it is in Box Preview:

Disabling Integration Activity

If you do not want Box to track your activities or display them to others in Box Preview, you can opt out of Integration Activity.

To opt out of Integration Activity:

  • From Box, in the upper-right portion of the screen, next to your initials click the down arrow.
  • From the menu that displays, click Account Settings.
  • When the Account Settings page displays, click the Integrations tab.
  • In the Integration Activity Stream section, check Hide my Integration Activity. Important

When you opt out from Integration Activity, the system hides all previous activities as well.

You can also delete from the Integration Activity stream any specific file action that you generated. You can do this directly from Box Preview. To do this:

  • In the Integration Activity stream, locate the file action you want to delete.
  • Next to the action, click the garbage can icon, and at the prompt, click Delete. Deleting a specific activity removes it from that file in Box. It also is no longer available to anyone else. However, this does not delete the activity from within the third-party application, itself. Others can still access the relevant conversation or record from within the individual app.

Tracking User Activity on Files

Box enables you to track user activity on virtually any file in two ways:

  • Recent activity, via avatars that display when you preview a file
  • Lifetime activity via Content Insights, which provide comprehensive file usage statistics you can view or download These features enable you quickly and easily to see who has accessed a file and the action they took on it.

Note

Tracking file activity is available only on the files of Starter, Business, Business Plus, and Enterprise accounts, and only are visible if you’re an owner, co-owner, or editor of the file. If the “Hide collaborators and their activity from non-owners” setting is turned on for a folder, owners and co-owners still see file activity, but editors do not. See Managing Collaborators for more information.

Tracking recent file activity via avatars

Depending on permissions (see the note above), Box displays avatars in the header of a file’s Preview page. Each avatar represents someone who, within the prior 30 days, has taken one of the following actions on the file:

  • edited
  • commented
  • previewed
  • downloaded Click on any avatar to display a list that gives you a visual, at-a-glance indication of who has been active recently in a file and what action they took. This can be useful in many ways – for example, if you’re working on a time-sensitive document in Box and you need it reviewed. Preview the file in Box and see immediately who accessed it and what they did, so you can send a reminder to anyone for whom you may still be waiting.

Here’s what it looks like when you preview a file:

Here’s a closer look, with the list displayed:

Note

Hovering over one avatar displays that person’s most recent action. Also, Box displays up to three avatars in the file preview page. If more than three people have acted upon the file within the past 30 days, Box displays the most recent three users and also a + sign indicating the number of additional people who’ve used the file. The limit is 103 people – that is, you won’t know if more than 103 people act on a within 30 days.

Note

Anonymous users – people who are not logged in to Box and access a file using a shared link – are not displayed in this recent activity indicator. However, they are included in the Content Insights feature detailed below.

Tracking lifetime file activity via Content Insights

“Content Insights” refers to the actions people take on a particular file. Box begins accruing these statistics the moment the file was uploaded, recording every time someone:

  • views the file
  • comments on the file
  • edits the file
  • downloads the file Content Insights, in essence, are a full audit log of all user activity on a file – who has accessed the file and what they did next. This can also be useful in many ways – for example, if you’re doing some folder cleanup. Use Content Insights to quickly view a file’s history; if no one’s accessed it in at least a year, you may consider deleting that file.

You can also export file usage statistics into a downloadable Excel spreadsheet.

Accessing Content Insights

Accessing Content Insights is easy: you can view Content Insights from either your Files window, or from within the file.

To view Content Insights from your Files window:

  • In your Box Files window, click next to a document’s title but don’t open the document.

  • In the right-hand Details sidebar, Box displays a summary of recent viewer activity.

  • To see further information, click See Details. To view Content Insights from within a file:

  • In your Box Files window, open a file. Box displays the file in the preview window.

  • Do one of the following:

    • At the top of the window, click the Content Insights icon. Box displays a summary of recent viewer activity.
    • Or, in the right sidebar, open the Details pane. Under Content Insights, Box displays a summary of recent viewer activity.

  • To see further information, click See Details. When you click See Details, the Content Insights window shows you totals for event types.

  • At the top of the Content Insights window, you can select to see events that have happened over the past week, month, quarter, or year.

  • In the Activity pane, you can search for viewer activities based on viewer, date, or activity type. Note

  • File editors will not get Content Insights if the folder-level setting Hide collaborators and their activity from non-owners is enabled. For more information on this setting, please review the article on Folder Settings. Box displays the user names only for users who access the file while logged in. For people who access the content through a public shared link without logging in, Box displays only their IP address (a set of numbers) and their location.

  • If your admin enabled Restrict Content Creation, only the primary admin and co-admin can export Content Insights reports.

  • Content Insights enables you to see activity in Box Notes, but because Box Notes cannot be downloaded, Content Insights always reports “0” downloads for Box Notes.

Understanding when “Someone” downloads your files

“Someone” is anyone who downloads a file from a shared link while not logged into Box. You receive these updates if you or one of your collaborators has enabled “Open Access” shared links to content you own or have access to.

“Someone” also displays if you’re collaborating in a folder that has the “Hide collaborators and their activity from non-owners” option turned on.

For added security reporting, admins of Business and Enterprise accounts can track the IP addresses associated with each notification referencing “Someone” within the Admin Console.

Exporting Content Insights

In addition to viewing Content Insights, you can also generate an export for further analysis.

Note

The ability to export data from Content Insights is available only on files owned by Business Plus and Enterprise accounts. It is not available to the following Box users:

  • Personal and Personal pro users
  • Non-admin users in enterprises that have enabled Restrict Content Creation. Notes:

Deleted user’s information [Name and Email]

If you run a report for less than a one-year, the deleted user’s information, including Name and Email, will not be available. These fields are shown as A prior collaborator. If you want a deleted user’s information, you can run the 1+ year report, which will populate these fields with the name and email ID of deleted users.

Access via an shared link

User Email displays A prior collaborator when someone who is not logged into Box accesses a file through a shared link.

To export Content Insights for a file:

  • In your Box Files window, open a file.
  • At the top of the window, click the Content Insights icon. Box displays a summary of recent viewer activity.
  • In the summary window, click See Details.
  • In the Activity pane, click Export All Activity and select the filters you want to apply.
    • Activity: By default, all event types will be included in the export, though you can choose to limit the export to specific event types.
    • Users or Groups: You can optionally limit the export to only include activity performed by certain users or groups of users.
    • Event Categories: A Content Insights report created for a duration less than one year will show limited categories of events, compared to the report exported for more than one year. The events will be limited to the events you see in the UI (Previews, Downloads, Edits, Comments).
      • If you want all the events (Previews, Download, Edit, Comment, File Opened, Edited user) and you are an Admin, use the User Activity Report.
      • If you want all the events (Previews, Download, Edit, Comment, File Opened, Edited user), and you are NOT an Admin, export a report for a duration of more than one year.
    • Date Range: By default, the export will be limited to events in the past day, though you can choose to include events from a longer time period, including All Time or a custom date range.
  • Once you’ve chosen your desired filters, click Create to generate the export. Box automatically uploads your exported report to the Box Reports folder in your account. (If this folder does not exist, Box automatically creates it before uploading your export.) tech_writers_swarm_kb

Tracking User Activity on Folders

Box enables folder owners to track activity in folders they own. Folder Insights allows a folder owner to see how many:

  • Internal and external collaborators exist for a folder
  • Shared links exist within the folder
  • Previews, downloads, uploads, and edits have occurred by collaborators within a defined time period Folder owners can also generate reports on any of the above.

Note:

  • Each user is limited to 10 downloads per report type each day. This means users may download up to 10 Folder Activity reports, 10 Collaborators reports, and 10 Shared Links reports daily, for a maximum total of 30 reports per user per day.
  • Reports are saved by default in the Box Reports folder, though you can select a different destination folder during the creation process. Learn more at Report Destination Folders.

Viewing Folder Insights

  • Select a folder.

  • Select More Options (), and then select Folder Insights. Folder Insights information is shown in a set of data tiles. They include:

  • Folder Activity

  • Collaborators

  • Shared Links

Folder Activity Tile

The Folder Activity tile contains a line chart that gives you detailed statistics from the past 90 days (default date range) about how folder collaborators are interacting with your content. To see how many collaborators interacted with files in the folder at any given time, move your pointer anywhere along the graph. You can toggle which type of activity you view in the chart by selecting an item in the legend.

Filtering Folder Activity Data

The buttons at the top of the tile are where you can select which collaborators to show in the chart and the date range for their activities.

For Collaborators, you can select:

  • All collaborators (default)

  • Internal collaborators

  • External collaborators For Date Range, you can select:

  • Last 30 days

  • Last 60 days

  • Last 90 days (default)

  • Custom range, and then select a start and end date

Downloading Folder Activity Data

The Download Report button () will generate a Folder Activity report of the data being currently viewed in the tile. When you generate a Folder Activity report, you select which folder you want the report saved to.

When downloading a report, you can select the report destination folder.

Collaborators Tile

The Collaborators tile is a donut charts that shows the number of collaborators that have been invited to the folder, grouped by internal and external collaborators. Hover over any segment of the donut chart to see a count of how many collaborators fall into each category. You can toggle which type of collaborators you view in the chart by selecting an item in the legend.

Downloading Collaborator Data

The Download Report button () will generate a Collaborator report of the data being currently viewed in the tile. When you generate a Collaborator report, you select which folder you want the report saved to.

Shared Links Tile

The Shared Links tile is a donut charts that shows the number of shared links that have created or any content within the folder, grouped by type of shared link. Hover over any segment of the donut chart to see a count of how many shared links fall into each category. You can toggle which type of shared links you view in the chart by selecting an item in the legend.

Downloading Shared Links Data

The Download Report button () will generate a Shared Links report of the data being currently viewed in the tile. When you generate a Shared Links report, you select which folder you want the report saved to.

Trash page not displayed

Issue

When going to the Trash page and selecting Items I Own, the user sees the following screen with no content displayed:

Root Cause

This error occurs when the user’s trash contains an excessive amount of items.

Resolution

In Search files and folders, you can select In Trash under In Folder to search for content within the Trash.

Additionally, adding “?usemarker=true” to the Trash page URL conditionally shows items in the Trash.

Example: https://<subdomain>.ent.box.com/trash?usemarker=true

However, note the following differences from the standard Trash page when using this URL:

  • You cannot sort items.
  • You cannot navigate directly to a specified page.
  • The Back button in Box does not work (you can still use your browser’s back button).
  • Content types (folders, files, bookmarks, etc.) are displayed in a mixed order, unlike the standard Trash view, where they are shown in the order of folders, files, and bookmarks.

Troubleshooting Content Preview - Previews Do Not Load

Overview of Problem

Some files may fail to preview due to conversion issues. This affects your ability to view file contents directly in Box. You will see a blank preview or an error message when attempting to preview the file.

Process for Resolution

  • Obtain a HAR File:
    • Open the browser’s developer tools (usually F12 or right-click and select “Inspect”).
    • Go to the “Network” tab.
    • Reproduce the issue.
    • Export the HAR for analysis.
    • Browser-specific instructions in How to Generate Network Captures for Troubleshooting.
  • Analyze the HAR capture:
    • Look for requests to the particular file ID’s “representations” endpoint.
    • Check if the conversion process is initially “pending”.
    • Verify if the last “representations” call shows that the conversion has failed.
  • Reupload the file:
    • Check if the file converts properly on the second try.

Outcome

  • The file should now preview correctly after reuploading.

Alternatives

  • If you continue to experience any of the symptoms listed above, open a support ticket at support.box.com for further assistance.

Troubleshooting Content Preview - Slow Preview Loading

Overview of Problem

Slow preview loading in Box can manifest as a generic icon or a spinning circle. This issue is caused by slow download speeds to dl.boxcloud.com, which can be due to environmental factors (e.g., international location) or network issues (e.g., firewall/proxy interference). It can also occur if the file is very large or complex, taking longer to load.

Process for Resolution

  • Check Network Issues:
    • Verify if there are any network settings affecting dl.boxcloud.com.
    • Use a tool like Ookla or a similar service to test the download speed.
  • Obtain a HAR File:
    • Open the browser’s developer tools (usually F12 or right-click and select “Inspect”).
    • Go to the “Network” tab.
    • Reproduce the issue and export the HAR file.
    • Browser-specific instructions in How to Generate Network Captures for Troubleshooting.
  • Reduce File Size:
    • If the file is very large or complex, use a tool like smallpdf.com to reduce its size.

Outcome

  • With network issues resolved or file sizes reduced, previews should load faster.

Alternatives

  • If network issues persist, contact your network administrator to check for firewall/proxy interference.
  • If the file is too large, consider splitting it into smaller parts or using a different format.
  • If you continue to experience any of the symptoms listed above, open a support ticket at support.box.com for further assistance.

Troubleshooting Uploads to Box

Summary

If you are having trouble uploading files or folders to Box using your web browser, Box Drive, or Box Mobile, this guide covers both quick self-service fixes and in-depth diagnostic steps.

You can match your exact error message in the Quick Diagnostic Guide below, or follow the detailed sections covering file naming restrictions, storage quotas, network firewalls, and upload performance.

  • Section 1: Storage Quota Exceeded: “Uploading this will put you over your allocated space” or “Account upload limit reached”
  • Section 2: Maximum File Size Limits: “File size exceeds limit” or large files fail immediately
  • Section 3: Network Errors, Firewalls, and Proxy Servers: “Network Error”, upload bar freezes at 99%, or “An error occurred with the upload. Please refresh the page and try again”
  • Section 4: File Name, Character, and Path Restrictions: “File name not supported” or “Value must be greater than or equal to 0”
  • Section 5: Uploading Empty Folders: Empty folders do not upload when using the “Folder Upload” button
  • Section 6: Active and Locked Files: “File is locked” or active program errors (such as Outlook .pst files)
  • Section 7: Potential Causes of Slow Uploads and Bandwidth: Uploads are very slow or take much longer than expected
  • Section 8: Specialized Upload Methods: Email to Folder or FTP

Initial Quick Checks

Before investigating deeper technical causes, complete these standard baseline checks:

  • Update your web browser: Ensure you are using the latest version of Chrome, Firefox, Safari, or Edge. Out-of-date browsers can cause upload failures.
  • Clear your browser’s cache: Cached files and cookies can occasionally disrupt session tokens. Clear your browser cache and cookies, restart the browser, and try uploading again.
  • Confirm supported operating systems: Make sure your device runs an officially supported operating system (Windows or macOS version).
  • Toggle upload method: In the Box Web App, try using the File upload button instead of Folder upload, or vice versa.
  • Check your network connection to Box. If connected to the internet with a wireless card, try a wired LAN connection. Check to see if the connection to the internet drops intermittently. If this is the case, we recommend the Folder upload method.
  • Try temporarily disabling or configuring your firewall to allow Box as a trusted site. You may find that your anti-virus software includes a built-in firewall that is impacting performance. If you are attempting to access Box from an office location and experience upload issues, then please contact your IT administrator or internal Help Desk.
  • Proxy servers may sometimes cause failed uploads. If you see the error message: An error occurred with the upload. Please refresh the page and try again. Please contact your IT department or Help Desk and ask them to check your proxy configuration.
  • Upload from a local drive instead of a network drive: If the files you are uploading reside on a mapped network drive, corporate file share, or external server, copy or drag them onto your local hard drive (such as your Desktop) first, then upload to Box. Uploading directly from a network drive introduces latency, file access locks, and connection instability that can cause uploads to stall or fail.

Section 1: Storage Quota Exceeded

The Symptom

You receive the error message: “Uploading this will put you over your allocated space” or “Action Failed: Quota Exceeded”.

Why This Happens

Box calculates and deducts uploaded storage from the account that owns the target folder, not the account uploading the file. Even if your enterprise plan provides unlimited storage:

  • If the user who created and owns the folder has an individual storage quota set by their Box Administrator, and that quota is reached, all uploads to that folder are blocked.
  • If you own the folder, your personal quota may be full, or your Box Trash may contain deleted items that still count toward your storage total.
How to Fix It
  • If you are an End User:
    • Open the folder in the Box Web App and check the Owner listed in the right-hand Sharing sidebar.
    • If you are the owner, open your Trash in the left sidebar, click the More Options (…) icon, and select Empty Trash to permanently clear deleted files.
    • If another user owns the folder, contact the folder owner or your internal IT Help Desk and let them know that the folder owner’s Box storage quota needs to be increased.
  • If you are a Box Administrator:
    • In the Admin Console, go to Users & Groups > Managed Users.
    • Search for the user who owns the folder and click their profile.
    • Under Edit User Account Details, review Storage Allotted. Select Unlimited (or enter a larger storage amount) and click Save.
    • For full details, see Resolving Account Storage Quota Errors.

Section 2: Maximum File Size Limits

The Symptom

An individual file fails to upload, or you receive a notification stating the file exceeds the maximum size allowed for your account.

How to Check Your Account Limit
  • Log into Box.
  • Click your account icon or initials in the upper-right corner.
  • Select Account Settings from the menu.
  • On the Account tab, scroll down to Account Details and review your Max file size.
File Size Limits by Account Tier

Each Box account tier enforces a maximum ceiling on the size of any single file:

Box Account Plan

Maximum Single File Size Limit

Free Personal

250 MB

Personal Pro

5 GB

Starter

2 GB

Business

5 GB

Business Plus

15 GB

Enterprise

50 GB

Enterprise Plus

150 GB

Enterprise Advanced

500 GB

Important Rule for Shared Folders: Shared folders enforce the single file size limit of the Folder Owner’s plan, regardless of the plan tier of the person uploading. For example, if an Enterprise user (50 GB limit) collaborates in a folder owned by a Free Personal account (250 MB limit), uploads to that folder cannot exceed 250 MB.

Application-Specific Upload Limits

Some Box applications enforce specific upload limits regardless of your enterprise plan:

  • Box Mobile App: 15 GB
  • Box Sync: 15 GB
  • Email Uploads (u.box.com): 50 MB (total email payload, roughly 35 MB raw file size)
How to Fix It
  • If your file exceeds your plan limit, compress the file into multiple zip archives, or split large media files.
  • If uploading to a shared folder owned by a free account, ask an Enterprise user in your organization to create the folder instead and invite the collaborators.

Section 3: Network Errors, Firewalls, and Proxy Servers

The Symptoms
  • The upload starts, but freezes partway through (frequently at 99%).
  • You receive: “Network Error” or “An error occurred with the upload. Please refresh the page and try again.”
Why This Happens

When uploading via a web browser, Box streams files in multi-megabyte binary chunks directly to upload.box.com. Corporate security gateways, proxy servers, and firewalls may allow standard web browsing but block or terminate continuous data uploads, especially when deep packet inspection (DPI) or SSL inspection is enabled.

Diagnostic Steps
  • Compare with Box Drive: Try uploading the file using the Box Drive desktop application. If Box Drive succeeds while the web browser fails, the issue is specific to your browser or web proxy configuration.
  • Test Off-Network / Mobile Hotspot: Temporarily disconnect from your corporate VPN or switch your computer to a mobile Wi-Fi hotspot. If the upload succeeds off-network, your corporate office firewall or proxy is blocking upload streams.
  • Check for Port 80 / Port 443 Non-Response: Uploads may fail even when initial preflight HTTP OPTIONS requests succeed. If subsequent HTTP POST or PUT calls receive no response or time out, network security hardware is intercepting the upload.
How to Fix It
  • Configure Firewall as Trusted: Configure third-party firewall software (such as ZoneAlarm, Windows Defender Firewall, or macOS firewall) to allow Box domains as trusted destinations.
  • Corporate Proxy and IT Configuration: Contact your IT Help Desk or network administrator to ensure proxy configurations and firewalls allow uninterrupted traffic to *.box.com, *.boxcdn.net, and specifically upload.box.com. Ensure SSL inspection is bypassed for upload endpoints.

Section 4: File Name, Character, and Path Restrictions

File Name Validity and Length

Check that the file name is valid. Box only supports file or folder names that are 255 characters or less. File names containing non-printable ascii, “/” or “", names with leading or trailing spaces, and the special names “.” and “..” are also unsupported. Box supports only Unicode Basic Multilingual Plane 0 (BMP) characters in file and folder names.ters.

Reserved Characters Not Allowed

The following characters cannot be used in file or folder names on Box:

  • < (less than)
  • > (greater than)
  • : (colon)
  • " (double quote)
  • / (forward slash)
  • \ (backslash)
  • | (vertical bar or pipe)
  • ? (question mark)
  • * (asterisk)
Case and Accent Insensitivity

File and folder names in Box are case-insensitive (no distinction between a and A) and accent-insensitive (no distinction between a and ă). You cannot have two items named Test and tèst in the same folder, because each item name must be unique within its directory.

Invisible Formatting Characters Stripped by Box

When you upload or create an item, Box automatically strips the following invisible formatting characters from the name and saves the remaining valid characters. If a name consists solely of these characters, it is rejected because no valid characters remain:

  • U+00AD SOFT HYPHEN
  • U+200B ZERO WIDTH SPACE
  • U+200E LEFT-TO-RIGHT MARK
  • U+200F RIGHT-TO-LEFT MARK
  • U+202A LEFT-TO-RIGHT EMBEDDING
  • U+202B RIGHT-TO-LEFT EMBEDDING
  • U+202C POP DIRECTIONAL FORMATTING
  • U+202D LEFT-TO-RIGHT OVERRIDE
  • U+202E RIGHT-TO-LEFT OVERRIDE
  • U+2060 WORD JOINER
  • U+2061 FUNCTION APPLICATION
  • U+2062 INVISIBLE TIMES
  • U+2063 INVISIBLE SEPARATOR
  • U+2064 INVISIBLE PLUS
  • U+2066 LEFT-TO-RIGHT ISOLATE
  • U+2067 RIGHT-TO-LEFT ISOLATE
  • U+2068 FIRST STRONG ISOLATE
  • U+2069 POP DIRECTIONAL ISOLATE
  • U+FEFF ZERO WIDTH NO-BREAK SPACE (byte order mark) (Note: Box does not remove U+200C ZERO WIDTH NON-JOINER or U+200D ZERO WIDTH JOINER, as those characters are required for certain languages and emoji sequences).
Windows 255-Character Path Length

Verify that the file or folder’s path on Windows machines is under the 255-character Windows limitation. Folder paths that exceed 255 characters may truncate the content’s name before uploading to Box.

  • For example: file names will be shortened to the ‘8.3’ convention and contain a tilde character ‘~’: Exampl~1.PDF
macOS AppleDouble Companion Files (.DS_STORE and ._filename)
  • If you see filenames containing .DS_STORE or starting with dot underscore as in: “._filename” this is caused by Mac OS X and is known as AppleDouble.
    • For an explanation how to clean each see these resources:
      • techrepublic.com
      • en.wikipedia.org
        • AppleDouble Example: If you have a file named MyDocument.txt, macOS might create a hidden companion file called ._MyDocument.txt.
Invalid Timestamps (“Value must be greater than or equal to 0”)

If a local file’s created or modified timestamp fields are empty, corrupted, or contain negative values, Box will return the error: “Value must be greater than or equal to 0”. Open the file in its native application, make a minor edit, and save it to refresh the operating system timestamps before uploading.

Section 5: Uploading Empty Folders

When you try to upload an empty folder using New Folder Upload in the Box web interface, the upload does not start and the folder isn’t uploaded. However, if you drag and drop the same empty folder into Box, it uploads successfully.

This behavior is due to limitations in most web browsers’ file selection tools. When you select an empty folder through the file picker dialog (used by “Folder Upload”), browsers usually don’t recognize it as a valid upload because there are no files inside. As a result, no data is sent to Box for processing.

Use drag & drop to move the folder into your Box window instead of using New Folder Upload.

Expected Behavior with “New Folder Upload”

When you attempt to upload an empty folder using the Folder Upload button in the web interface, the upload will not start and the empty folder is not uploaded.

Why This Happens

This behavior is caused by limitations in web browser file selection dialogs. When you select an empty folder through a standard browser picker dialog, the browser does not recognize it as a valid data upload because it contains zero files. As a result, the browser transmits no data to Box.

The Solution: Use Drag and Drop

To upload an empty folder, drag and drop the empty folder directly from your computer desktop or file explorer into the Box web browser window. Drag and drop bypasses the browser file picker limitation and successfully creates the empty folder structure in Box.

Section 6: Active and Locked Files

The Symptom

The upload fails, or your computer displays an alert stating the file is in use or locked.

Why This Happens

Programs that continuously write data, such as Microsoft Outlook holding .pst archives, CAD software, or local database files, place exclusive system locks on files while open. Box cannot read or upload files that are locked by an active process.

How to Fix It
  • Save your work and close the application using the file.
  • If uploading an Outlook .pst file, quit Outlook completely and verify in Windows Task Manager that OUTLOOK.EXE has terminated.
  • If the file must remain open in another program, create a copy of the file on your local desktop and upload the copy instead.

Section 7: Potential Causes of Slow Uploads and Bandwidth

Bandwidth and Box Processing

Box does not limit, throttle, cap, or shape upload bandwidth.

Box does perform virus scanning, thumbnail generation, and metadata indexing on each file, which can affect the total completion time when uploading large numbers of files, but this does not limit the bits per second of your network connection.

For more information, please review our Fair Use Policy.

Upload speed depends on your network connection and a component of this is bandwidth.

  • Bandwidth determines the amount of data that can pass from the Internet to your web browser in a given amount of time.
  • A smaller bandwidth results in a longer time that it takes Internet data to transfer on your web browser. Box offers multiple endpoints to make sure your uploads (and downloads) are taking the most efficient route. See our announcement: Box expands its Global Network Presence

If you find that your upload is taking longer than it should, we have listed a few reasons that may affect upload speeds.

  • Firewalls: Firewalls can slow down or block the upload process. If you use third-party software, try temporarily turning off firewalls such as ZoneAlarm, the built-in Windows firewall, Mac firewall, or any others.
    • Simply configuring your firewall to allow the Box domains will likely solve this issue.
    • If uploads are failing even when OPTIONS calls are shown to succeed, please next check if the POST/PUT calls show a non-response on Port :80. This confirms that the actual upload attempt is being met with a non-response, and the firewall and other network configuration settings should be reviewed to find where this is failing.
  • Business network restrictions: Users accessing Box from an office setting may find that their IT department has blocked or slowed down connections to Box. VPNs can be the cause of slower connections.
    • If you are unsure whether your IT department has placed restrictions on uploads or unapproved websites, you can try connecting to Box from a different location, such as a coffee shop with Wi-Fi, to see if the issue persists. If the issue does not persist, then it is likely that your IT department has placed restrictions on Box.
    • If you’re using a VPN, your IP address may be misplaced, which can inadvertently put your computer in a different geographic location from your actual location. This can affect your upload speeds. Check with your network or IT department to see if a VPN is causing your computer to be placed in a different geographic location on the internet.
  • Browser Specific Issues: If you’re having trouble uploading files to Box, try using a different browser or computer. Some users find that their upload speeds increase when using a different browser or a faster computer..
  • Device Specific Issues: If your upload speed has not improved after trying different browsers and updating your browser, try using a different computer to isolate the issue.
    • If your upload speed increases on another computer, then the first computer is causing the slow speed.
    • If your speed does not increase, then it is likely an issue with your internet connection.
  • Internet Service Provider: Sometimes slow upload speeds are the fault of your Internet Service Provider.
    • We recommend a high-speed internet connection with high upload speeds. Fiber is best, followed by Cable and DSL.
    • Often with Cable and DSL, the upload speed is significantly slower than the download speed. This will result in fast loading times for most websites and file downloads, but slow uploads. A Note on Megabytes vs. Megabits:

There is a difference between “Mb” (megabit) and “MB” (megabyte). One megabyte is equal to eight megabits. Internet service providers (ISP) advertise upload and download speeds in terms of “Mbps” (megabits per second) while Box uploads are shown in your browser in terms of “MBps” (MegaBytes per second). So, if you see browser upload speeds of 15 MBps this would be interpreted as 125 Mbps by your ISP.

Section 8: Specialized Upload Methods

If you use automated or protocol-specific upload tools:

  • Email Upload to a Folder (u.box.com):
    • You can email attachments directly to a folder address formatted as upload.&lt;folder>.&lt;token>@u.box.com.
    • Total message size (email body plus all attachments) cannot exceed 50 MB (approximately 35 MB on disk before email encoding).
    • In Folder Settings, verify whether Allow uploads from anyone is enabled, or ensure the sending address is invited as a collaborator.
    • If using the Email Upload feature, then please review these for help:
      • Upload to Box Through Email
      • Email Uploads to a Folder Are Failing
      • Troubleshooting Email Uploads to Box Folders
  • FTP and FTPS:
    • FTP access is supported on Business, Business Plus, and Enterprise accounts.
    • Use passive mode (PASV) and explicit FTPS on port 21. Single file size limits match your account plan ceiling. webapp_swarm_kb

Unable to Access Content - User Signed into Wrong Account

If you are having trouble accessing a file or folder that has been shared with you, verify that you are signed in to the same Box account that the collaboration invite was sent to.

Organizations will set up Box accounts for their users with particular email addresses. User’s Box email addresses may not be the same as the email addresses they use to access their email inboxes.

Example:

  • A user’s box account email address is: janedoe@domain.com.
  • Their email inbox is signed into jdoe@domain.com.
  • They are invited to a folder using the email janedoe@domain.com and accept the invite from their inbox.
  • They will receive the error below in their Box account

To rectify this, please follow the steps below:

  • Confirm which email the invitation is being sent to.
  • Check which email address your Box account is associated to. To do so, go to your Box account, click on your name on the top right hand side, then navigate to “Account Settings.”
  • Make sure the email address the invitation was sent to matches the email in your account settings.
  • If they do not match, have the invitation sent to the email associated with the Box account. If the emails match up and you still get this error message for items you are invited to collaborate in, please open a case with our User Services team.

Note: Please ensure that all collaborations are sent to your primary Box email address and not to your secondary email address if you have one tied to your account. This can also cause the issue above to occur.

webapp_swarm_kb

Unable to bulk delete folders or files in the trash

Issue

When clicking Delete All to remove folders from the trash, an error may occur with the following message: “We could not perform this action because the designated folder is locked by another operation.”

Root Cause

Clicking Delete All for the trash will simultaneously delete all the folders or files in the Trash.

If the trash contains parent-child folders, the system will attempt to delete the parent folder while the deletion of its child folder is still in progress. This prevents locking the parent folder and results in an error.

Resolution

If the trash contains parent-child folders, you can delete them in the following two ways:

  • Delete child folders first, then click Delete All again to remove the remaining folders.
  • Instead of Delete All, select specific folders or files to delete individually. If the issue persists after 24 hours, please contact Box Support.

Unable to create editable shared links

Issue

Attempting to create a shared link for a file with its publication range set to Can edit results in causing the following error message, preventing the operation from being completed:

“Editable shared links have been restricted by the admin or owner of this item.”

Root Cause

This error occurs because the creation of editable shared links is restricted by the tenant settings or the file owner’s settings.

Resolution

To enable the creation of editable shared links, the following two settings need to be configured:

  • In the tenant where the file is located, navigate to Admin Console > Enterprise Settings > Content & Sharing tab > Shared Link, and under Shared Link Permissions, select “Can view, download, and edit” as the actions that link recipients can take on the file.
  • support.box.com
  • In the file owner’s settings, navigate to Account Settings > Share tab > Shared Link, and select “Preview, download and edit the shared item” as the actions that link recipients can take.
  • support.box.com

Unable to Create Shared Link with Certain Access Level

With Shared Links, there are three default access levels that you can choose:

  • People with the Link: Anyone that has the URL can access the file.
  • People in my Company: Any Box User with your company email domain and that is logged into their account can access.
  • People in this Folder: Any Box User collaborated on the folder you are sharing or the folder that contains the file you are sharing can access. However, some users may not see the option to create a Shared Link at one of these levels.

Troubleshooting Steps

  • Make sure that the Shared Link access level is enabled at the Enterprise level.
    • If you are not an Admin, please reach out to your account’s Admin or Company IT team to check this setting.
  • Check your Account Settings > Sharing settings to make sure you’ve enabled the problem access level for your own account.
    • It is possible to limit your own sharing settings further than what is required by the Admin.
  • If you do not have the “People in [Company Name]” option, make sure your Box account has your company’s email domain listed. You will want to reach out to an Administrator if you are not one for this step.
    • To set a company-level domain, we must have at least one email domain attached to your account. Otherwise, we cannot easily verify a user’s “in company” status. webapp_swarm_kb

Unable to create, delete, copy, or move folders

Issue

Attempting a folder operation results in an error.

  • When creating/deleting a folder
  • When copying a folder
  • Click Details
  • When moving a folder
  • Click Details

Root Cause

One of the following can cause this error:

  • The API has locked the folder deletion or movement.
  • Another folder operation is interfering with the process.
  • If a large-scale folder operation is in progress, actions on the source and destination folders, as well as their parent and subfolders, are restricted. To identify the cause of the error, follow the steps described below.

To obtain network logs, refer to: support.box.com

When the API has locked the folder deletion or movement:

  • When deleting a folder

  • The following code appears for the “delete” request in the network log.

    {     “status”: 403,     “errorCode”: “freezeLocked”,     “data”: “This folder cannot be moved or deleted because it has been locked to prevent such operations.” }

  • When moving a folder

  • The error details show the message: “This folder cannot be moved or deleted because it has been locked to prevent such operations.” If another folder operation is interfering:

  • When creating a folder

  • The following code appears for the “create” request in the network log.

    {     “status”: 400,     “errorCode”: “createFolderGeneralError”,     “data”: {            “message”: “Folder is locked by another operation.”     } }

  • When deleting a folder

  • The following code appears for the “delete” request in the network log.

    {     “status”: 409,     “errorCode”: “operationInProgressError”,     “data”: “A conflicting operation is being performed on one or more of the selected items.” }

  • When copying a folder

  • The error details show the message: “You cannot copy this folder because either the source or destination folder is currently locked by another operation.”

  • When moving a folder

  • The error details show the message: “You cannot move this folder because either this folder or the destination folder is locked by another operation.”

Resolution

When the API has locked the folder deletion or movement:

Check the folder status via the Folder Lock API and unlock the folder as necessary. For details of the Folder Lock API, refer to: developer.box.com

If another folder operation is interfering:

The issue depends on the progress of the large-scale folder operation causing the error. If you are still unable to perform any operations after 24 hours, please contact our customer support.

Understand the Maximum File Size You Can Upload to Box

The maximum file size limit for uploads to Box varies depending on your account type:

  • Free personal: 250 MB
  • Personal Pro: 5 GB
  • Starter: 2 GB
  • Business: 5 GB
  • Business Plus: 15 GB
  • Enterprise (and Digital Suites ): 50 GB
  • Enterprise Plus: 150 GB
  • Enterprise Advanced: 500GB For more details, refer to Box Plans & Pricing.

IMPORTANT: On January 13, 2025, Box increased Shuttle’s maximum file size for Enterprise Advanced accounts from 150 GB to 500 GB. Because a job’s maximum file size is automatically set when the job is created, in jobs created before January 13, 2025, file uploads over 150 GB still fail. To mitigate these upload failures, create new jobs for the affected files.

To confirm the file size limit for your account:

  • Log into Box.
  • Click your account icon in the upper-right-hand corner.
  • Select Account Settings from the menu that displays.
  • Scroll down to the Account details and review your Max file size listed. Application-specific upload limits

Some Box apps have lower application-specific limits, regardless of what plan you have purchased. See the following for reference:

  • Box Mobile: 15GB
  • Box Sync: 15GB
  • Email Uploads: 50MB How these upload limits are enforced

Be aware shared folders enforce the file size limit that applies to the Folder Owner’s plan, regardless of whether any of the collaborators within the folder have a higher limit.

Here’s an example: Someone with a business account uploads files to a shared folder owned by someone with a free Box account. In this case, the business account holder is limited to uploads of 250 MB or fewer, since the folder belongs to the free account holder.

Alternatively, a free user collaborating on a folder owned by an Enterprise User can upload files of up to 50 GB in size in this folder.

Understanding Box File Timestamps

The frequently asked questions about Box file timestamps are answered in this article:

  • What are Box file timestamps?
  • What timestamps does Box display for each file?
  • Does Box preserve Created and Modified timestamps when uploading content to Box?
  • Where are the file timestamps visible?
  • What file operations affect the Modified timestamps?
  • What file operations do not affect the Modified timestamps?
  • When I add a new file version, what timestamps are affected?
  • Are timestamps preserved when downloading files from Box?
  • Is the timestamp affected when I delete a file or restore a file from trash?
  • What timestamp is displayed if one of my files does not have an associated timestamp for the Created and Modified operations?
  • How does Box Drive handle timestamps for synced files?
  • How does Box Sync handle timestamps for synced files?
  • How do the Box APIs handle timestamp displays?

What are Box file timestamps?

Box records file times and dates when files are created, modified, or uploaded on Box.

Box stores timestamp values in UTC format, so they are not affected by changes in time zone or daylight saving time.

What timestamps does Box display for each file?

Box displays the following timestamps for each file operation:

  • Created: The timestamp when the file was created.
  • This timestamp display does not change if you save or modify this file.
  • Modified: The timestamp when the contents of a file were last modified.
  • Uploaded: The timestamp when the file was uploaded to Box. This timestamp display changes for each uploaded version.
  • Updated: The timestamp when the file was last changed in Box (Modified or Uploaded). The timestamp display does not change when you open, close, view, or rename a file.

Does Box preserve Created and Modified timestamps when uploading content to Box?

The timestamps are preserved based on the file upload method and protocol as described in the following table.

Caution: Be aware that some browsers are affiliated with particular upload mechanisms like HTML, or Ajax.

Box Upload Method

Folders: No, a folder’s “Modified” timestamp is the date when the folder is created on Box.

Where are the file timestamps visible?

Box file timestamp information is displayed in several locations:

  • Web application: The File Properties window displays the Created and Modified timestamps.
  • To view this information: right-click on a file or click the ellipses button (…), then select Properties and click File Information.
  • Box Sync: Your local file system displays the Created or Modified timestamps in the Finder or Explorer window for newly-synced files.

What file operations affect the Modified timestamps?

The Modified timestamp changes when you edit the contents of a file.

What file operations do not affect the Modified timestamps?

The Modified timestamp does not change when you perform any of the following file operations:

  • Preview or download a file
  • Add, update, or delete comments/tasks/file descriptions
  • Share or unshare a link
  • Send a shared or direct link
  • Open, close, or rename a file

When I add a new file version, what timestamps are affected?

The following list identifies the affected timestamps each time you add a new file version:

  • Created: The new version does not affect the Created timestamp.
  • Modified: The new version reflects the Modified timestamp for this file version.
  • Uploaded: The new version reflects the Uploaded timestamp for this file version.

Are timestamps preserved when downloading files from Box?

When you download a single file, the created and modified date is not preserved, rather it will be set to the time of download.

When you download multiple files from Box, the selected files (folders) are downloaded to your computer as a ZIP file. The Modified timestamp for each file (or files within a folder) is set to the same timestamp as when the content was last modified in Box.

Each ZIP client handles the uncompressed timestamp information differently. See your ZIP client documentation for further details.

You can also use the Box API to obtain file timestamp information.

Is the timestamp affected when I delete a file or restore a file from trash?

If you delete a file and restore it from trash at a later date, there is no change to the timestamp. Box continues to maintain the timestamp of the file and restores it seamlessly.

What timestamp is displayed if one of my files does not have an associated timestamp for the Created and Modified operations?

If a file does not have a created timestamp or the modified timestamp after it is uploaded to Box, then Box uses the timestamp when this file was first uploaded to Box.

Similarly, if your local device cannot pass the timestamp, then Box uses the timestamp when this file was first uploaded to Box.

How does Box Drive handle timestamps for synced files?

All files visible to you have the correct Date Modified timestamps.

Local folders’ Date Modified often do not match the Date Modified of the folder on Box. The local folder’s Date Modified is updated only after the following actions:

  • A file inside the folder is updated (opened and changed) locally.
  • A folder inside the folder is modified (renamed for example) locally.
  • A new folder is created inside the folder locally.

How does Box Sync handle timestamps for synced files?

Effective Release 4.0.4376, Box Sync preserves the created and modified timestamps when downloading files from Box. Additionally, when a file is added to Box Sync via the desktop, the created and modified timestamps for each file are also visible via the web application.

Box Sync preserves timestamps when content changes on Box or in your local file system, sending timestamps to Box during uploads, and setting timestamps on the local file system during downloads.

If a timestamp changes without the file’s content changing, the new timestamp won’t be applied to the other file system.

How do the Box APIs handle timestamp displays?

See the developer documentation for more information on timestamps used in Box APIs. All information provided in this article also applies to timestamp displays using Box APIs.

Notes and conditions

The numbered notes below correspond to the superscript numbers in the permissions table. They are grouped by category so you can skip sections that don’t apply to you.

Role-specific behavior
  • Comment deletion: Comments can be deleted only by the folder owner, co-owner, or the person who created the comment.
  • Annotation limits for Previewers: Previewers and Previewer Uploaders can create annotations but cannot highlight and comment.
  • Annotation deletion: Annotations can be deleted by owners and co-owners of the folder containing the annotated document, as well as by the annotation creator.
  • Copy for Viewers: Viewers can download a file and re-upload it elsewhere, or use Ctrl+C / Ctrl+V to copy a file to another folder they have access to.
  • Copy for Viewer Uploaders: Viewer Uploaders can only copy using keyboard shortcuts. The Copy option does not appear in the context menu.
  • File Request Link: Currently applies only to the enhanced version of File Request.
Scope and ownership
  • Deleting files and folders: Co-owners and editors can delete sub-folders but not root-level folders. Only owners can delete folders at the root level. If a co-owner attempts to delete a root folder, they receive an option to End Collaboration. Co-owners and editors can permanently delete collaborated content from trash if the owner’s trash settings permit and the content is not retained by a policy.
  • Moving content: Co-owners and editors can move only content within the folder they are collaborating on. For example, if a collaborator is invited to Folder A (which contains Folder B and File C), they can move Folder B and File C but cannot move the top-level Folder A itself.
  • Box Item: When you create a Box Item, Box enables you to define a custom scope for it.
Admin-configurable settings
  • Offline access for Previewers (mobile): Previewers can save files for offline use on Box Mobile only if the “Preview only” collaborators can save files for offline use toggle is enabled in Admin Console > Enterprise Settings > Mobile.
  • Editor invitation restrictions: If Enterprise-level and folder-level permissions are restricted, editors cannot invite collaborators.
  • Content insights visibility: If the Hide collaborators and their activity from non-owners setting is turned on for a folder, owners and co-owners still see file activity but editors do not. See Managing Collaborators for details. If the admin has enabled the Restrict Content Creation setting, only the primary admin and co-admin can export access stats reports.

Role descriptions

Available on all accounts

Editor: Full read/write access to a folder or file. Editors can view, download, upload, edit, delete, copy, move, rename, generate and edit shared links, make comments, assign tasks, create tags, and invite or remove collaborators. Editors cannot copy, delete, or move root-level folders.

Viewer: Read access to a folder or file. Viewers can preview, download, make comments, and generate shared links. Viewers cannot add tags, invite new collaborators, edit shared links, upload, edit files, or delete items.

Shared link behavior for Viewers:

  • A Viewer cannot change who can access a shared link.
  • If no shared link exists, the Viewer can only create one with the folder owner’s default shared link setting.
  • If a shared link already exists, the Viewer can only share it at the access level currently set (for example, a Viewer cannot change a link set to “people with the link” to “people in the company”).
  • If a collaborator holds multiple permission sets, the least restrictive set takes precedence. For example, a Viewer who accesses a shared link set to allow Edit access gets Edit rights on that item.
Available on Business and Enterprise accounts

An admin must enable these permission levels in Admin Console > Enterprise Settings > Content & Sharing > Collaborating on Content. These roles apply only to folders; single-file collaborations support only Editor and Viewer.

Co-owner: All the read/write access of an Editor, plus the ability to change some advanced folder settings. Co-owners cannot change the owner of a folder.

Previewer: Limited read access. Previewers can only preview items using the integrated content viewer. They can use the browser’s search function to search text in content, but cannot use the file-specific search. Previewers cannot select and copy text, share, upload, edit, or delete content.

Uploader: Limited write access. Uploaders can upload content and see item names in a folder, but cannot download or view content.

Note: In Hubs, if a folder Uploader is invited to a Hub as Viewer, the folder Uploader’s permissions change to Viewer Uploader.

Viewer Uploader: A combination of Viewer and Uploader. Full read access and limited write access. Viewer Uploaders can preview, download, add comments, generate shared links, and upload content. They cannot add tags, invite collaborators, or delete items. They can edit files through Box Edit (download, edit, and re-upload seamlessly) or manually by downloading, editing locally, and re-uploading with the same file name. Viewer Uploaders cannot modify file names or delete files.

Previewer Uploader: A combination of Previewer and Uploader. Limited read and write access. Previewer Uploaders can preview, add comments, add tasks, and upload content. They cannot add tags, generate shared links, invite collaborators, select and copy text, or edit or delete items.
